literature.headline_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期乙型肝炎病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 10 岁时,六价组的血清保护(抗 HBs ≥ 10 mIU/mL)为 75.8%,五价组为 32.8%。在整个随访过程中,六价组的几何平均浓度仍然高出一个对数。所有儿童 10 岁时的抗 HBc 检测均为阴性,表明没有突破性感染的血清学证据。 [10.1080/21645515.2026.2765983]
这篇综述将 RNA 干扰 (RNAi) 平台总结为新兴疗法。通过靶向 共价闭合环状DNA 和整合的 HBV DNA 的转录本,它们比当前的 抗病毒药物 具有机械优势。与衣壳组装调节剂、聚乙二醇化 IFN、治疗性 疫苗 或反义药物的组合可产生抗原的累加或协同下降,支持 RNAi 作为治疗性多药方案的支柱。 [10.1080/1750743x.2026.2769254]
所提供的证据没有明确陈述稳定的共识或中心结论。 [10.1080/14656566.2026.2768090]
在中位 治疗 持续时间 14.7 年中,98 名患者发展为 HCC。低基线 qHBsAg 水平(< 10,000 IU/mL)与高基线 qHBsAg 水平(≥ 10,000 IU/mL)相比,与 HCC 风险高三到四倍显着相关。 [10.1007/s12072-026-11157-6]
在这项研究中,我们通过之前报道的GLP-26的结构优化发现了化合物39(命名为XT1061),其在体外表现出有效的抗HBV活性(EC50 = 1.0 ± 0.1 nM)。 [10.1021/acs.jmedchem.6c01941]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: At 10 years of age, seroprotection (anti-HBs ≥ 10 mIU/mL) was 75.8% in the hexavalent group and 32.8% in the pentavalent group. The geometric mean concentrations remained one log higher in the hexavalent group throughout follow-up. [10.1080/21645515.2026.2765983]

This review summarizes RNA interference (RNAi) platforms as emerging therapies. By targeting transcripts from both cccDNA and integrated HBV DNA, they offer a mechanistic advantage over current antivirals. [10.1080/1750743x.2026.2769254]
The supplied evidence does not clearly state a stable consensus or central conclusion. [10.1080/14656566.2026.2768090]

Over a 14.7-year median treatment duration, 98 patients developed HCC. A low baseline qHBsAg level (< 10,000 IU/mL) was significantly associated with a three to four times higher risk of HCC than a high baseline qHBsAg level (≥ 10,000 IU/mL). [10.1007/s12072-026-11157-6]

HBV-ACLF patients showed profound peripheral immune remodeling, characterized by a pro-inflammatory shift toward M1-like monocyte/macrophage polarization, accompanied by compensatory upregulation of M2-like monocytes/macrophages and a sharp increase in serum TNF-α, interferon-gamma, and interleukin (IL)-6 (all FDR-adjusted P < 0.05). [10.4254/wjh.125101]

papers.title: The Safety, Pharmacokinetics, and Antiviral Activity of ABI-4334, A Novel Next-Generation Hepatitis B Capsid Assembly Modulator.
papers.abstract: Novel, well-tolerated, short-term therapeutics for chronic hepatitis B virus infection (cHBV) are needed. ABI-4334 is a next-generation capsid assembly modulator that targets the HBV core protein. The safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of ABI-4334 in healthy volunteers and participants with cHBV and antiviral effects in participants with cHBV were examined in two Phase 1 studies. Study 101 was a placebo-controlled study of healthy volunteers that included four single-ascending dose cohorts and two once-daily multiple-ascending dose cohorts randomized 6:2 (ABI-4334:placebo), and one crossover food-effect cohort randomized 3:3 (fed:fasted). Study 102 was a randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled study where participants with cHBV were randomized 8:2 (ABI-4334 [2 dose cohorts]:placebo). Overall, 54 healthy volunteers and 20 participants with cHBV were included in Studies 101 and 102, respectively. Most participants (75%) in Study 102 were hepatitis B e antigen (HBeAg) negative and generally had lower baseline HBV DNA and pregenomic RNA (pgRNA) levels. ABI-4334 was well tolerated, with no treatment-emergent serious adverse events (AEs) or treatment-emergent AEs leading to study discontinuation. The mean ABI-4334 plasma half-life ranges were comparable across doses in both studies. Following multiple-dose administration in participants with cHBV, the steady-state mean plasma half-life ranged from 17.5 to 27.5 h. HBV DNA declines were observed in both HBeAg-positive (n = 3) and -negative (n = 13) participants across doses. Reductions in pgRNA were observed in participants with detectable pgRNA at baseline. ABI-4334 was well tolerated, with pharmacokinetics and antiviral results supporting the continued development of ABI-4334 as a monotherapy or component of novel combination regimens for cHBV. Trial Registration: Study 101 (NCT05569941). Study 102 (NCT06384131).

papers.title: Waning of hepatitis B surface antibody but no serological evidence of breakthrough infection up to 10 years of age after hexavalent and pentavalent vaccination in infancy.
papers.abstract: Thailand incorporated the hepatitis B (HepB) vaccine into infant combination vaccines. The current available formulations are pentavalent (DTwP-HB-Hib) and hexavalent (DTaP-IPV-HB-Hib) vaccines. The national policy recommends these combination vaccines at 2, 4, and 6 months of age, following a monovalent HepB vaccine at birth. In this study, sera samples of a randomized cohort of children who received hexavalent or pentavalent vaccines at 2, 4, 6, and 18 months were collected (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02408926). This cohort received one more HepB dose than the national schedule (total 5 doses). We evaluated the kinetics of anti-HBs and screened for evidence of breakthrough HepB infection using antibody to HepB core antigen (anti-HBc). Anti-HBs was measured annually from 2 through 10 years of age, and anti-HBc was tested at 10 years. A total of 153 children completed the study at age 10 years. Seroprotection (anti-HBs ≥ 10 mIU/mL) at 10 years was 75.8% in the hexavalent group vs. 32.8% in the pentavalent group, with geometric mean concentrations remaining one log higher in the hexavalent group throughout follow-up. Despite the waning of anti-HBs, all children tested negative for anti-HBc at 10 years. This indicates no serological evidence of breakthrough infection, even in children with anti-HBs < 10 mIU/mL.

papers.title_original: Waning of hepatitis B surface antibody but no serological evidence of breakthrough infection up to 10 years of age after hexavalent and pentavalent vaccination in infancy.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the kinetics of hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) and screen for evidence of breakthrough hepatitis B infection following hexavalent and pentavalent vaccination in infancy. The background highlights the incorporation of the hepatitis B vaccine into infant combination vaccines in Thailand.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A randomized cohort study was conducted on children who received hexavalent or pentavalent vaccines at 2, 4, 6, and 18 months of age. Sera samples were collected from these children for analysis.
analysis.methods: Anti-HBs levels were measured annually from 2 through 10 years of age, and anti-HBc was tested at 10 years to screen for breakthrough infection.
analysis.main_results: At 10 years of age, seroprotection (anti-HBs ≥ 10 mIU/mL) was 75.8% in the hexavalent group and 32.8% in the pentavalent group. The geometric mean concentrations remained one log higher in the hexavalent group throughout follow-up. All children tested negative for anti-HBc at 10 years, indicating no serological evidence of breakthrough infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that despite the waning of anti-HBs levels, there was no evidence of breakthrough hepatitis B infection in the cohort, even among those with anti-HBs below the protective threshold.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide important insights into the long-term effectiveness of hexavalent and pentavalent vaccines in preventing hepatitis B infection, which can inform vaccination strategies and surveillance efforts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's design is limited by its reliance on serological markers without direct virological confirmation of infection. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the follow-up and the potential for unmeasured confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the long-term antibody response and evidence of breakthrough hepatitis B infection in children vaccinated with hexavalent or pentavalent vaccines in infancy. The research aimed to evaluate the kinetics of anti-HBs and screen for breakthrough infection using anti-HBc testing. The study found that seroprotection at 10 years was higher in the hexavalent group, with geometric mean concentrations remaining one log higher throughout follow-up. Notably, all children tested negative for anti-HBc, indicating no serological evidence of breakthrough infection. These findings suggest that the vaccines are effective in preventing hepatitis B infection over a decade, even as anti-HBs levels wane. However, the study's reliance on serological markers and lack of direct virological confirmation limit the strength of the evidence, suggesting a moderate confidence level in the results.

papers.source_body_en: Thailand incorporated the hepatitis B (HepB) vaccine into infant combination vaccines. The current available formulations are pentavalent (DTwP-HB-Hib) and hexavalent (DTaP-IPV-HB-Hib) vaccines. The national policy recommends these combination vaccines at 2, 4, and 6 months of age, following a monovalent HepB vaccine at birth. In this study, sera samples of a randomized cohort of children who received hexavalent or pentavalent vaccines at 2, 4, 6, and 18 months were collected (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02408926). This cohort received one more HepB dose than the national schedule (total 5 doses). We evaluated the kinetics of anti-HBs and screened for evidence of breakthrough HepB infection using antibody to HepB core antigen (anti-HBc). Anti-HBs was measured annually from 2 through 10 years of age, and anti-HBc was tested at 10 years. A total of 153 children completed the study at age 10 years. Seroprotection (anti-HBs ≥ 10 mIU/mL) at 10 years was 75.8% in the hexavalent group vs. 32.8% in the pentavalent group, with geometric mean concentrations remaining one log higher in the hexavalent group throughout follow-up. Despite the waning of anti-HBs, all children tested negative for anti-HBc at 10 years. This indicates no serological evidence of breakthrough infection, even in children with anti-HBs < 10 mIU/mL.

papers.title: RNA interference and antisense strategies for chronic hepatitis B: mechanisms, clinical advances, and pathways toward functional cure.
papers.abstract: Current Chronic Hepatitis B (CHB) therapies, nucleos(t)ide analogs and interferon (IFN), suppress viral replication but cannot eliminate covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) or integrated HBV DNA, leaving CHB a global health threat. High antigen levels cause profound immune exhaustion, so agents must silence viral transcripts while restoring antiviral immunity. This review summarizes RNA interference (RNAi) platforms as emerging therapies. Preclinical and phase I-II data show that GalNAc-conjugated siRNAs (xalnesiran, imdusiran, elebsiran, daplusiran/tomligisiran, RBD-1016) reduce HBsAg by 1-2 log IU/mL, often for months after treatment. By targeting transcripts from both cccDNA and integrated HBV DNA, they offer a mechanistic advantage over current antivirals. Combinations with capsid assembly modulators, pegylated IFN, therapeutic vaccines, or antisense drugs yield additive or synergistic declines in antigen, supporting RNAi as a backbone for curative multidrug regimens. Despite promising safety and efficacy, obstacles remain: HBsAg plateaus, incomplete immune restoration, delivery challenges in advanced liver disease, and lack of biomarkers for patient selection. Nevertheless, RNAi therapies represent a paradigm-shifting strategy that could move CHB care toward a finite, immune-driven functional cure. A literature search was conducted using Google Scholar for articles on RNAi and antisense strategies for CHB (1985-2026).

papers.title_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎 的 RNA 干扰和反义策略:机制、临床进展和通往 功能性治愈 的途径。
papers.source_body_en: Current Chronic Hepatitis B (CHB) therapies, nucleos(t)ide analogs and interferon (IFN), suppress viral replication but cannot eliminate covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) or integrated HBV DNA, leaving CHB a global health threat. High antigen levels cause profound immune exhaustion, so agents must silence viral transcripts while restoring antiviral immunity. This review summarizes RNA interference (RNAi) platforms as emerging therapies. Preclinical and phase I-II data show that GalNAc-conjugated siRNAs (xalnesiran, imdusiran, elebsiran, daplusiran/tomligisiran, RBD-1016) reduce HBsAg by 1-2 log IU/mL, often for months after treatment. By targeting transcripts from both cccDNA and integrated HBV DNA, they offer a mechanistic advantage over current antivirals. Combinations with capsid assembly modulators, pegylated IFN, therapeutic vaccines, or antisense drugs yield additive or synergistic declines in antigen, supporting RNAi as a backbone for curative multidrug regimens. Despite promising safety and efficacy, obstacles remain: HBsAg plateaus, incomplete immune restoration, delivery challenges in advanced liver disease, and lack of biomarkers for patient selection. Nevertheless, RNAi therapies represent a paradigm-shifting strategy that could move CHB care toward a finite, immune-driven functional cure. A literature search was conducted using Google Scholar for articles on RNAi and antisense strategies for CHB (1985-2026).

papers.title: Hepatitis B and D: Interferon-Based Therapy-For Clinical Trials or Standard of Care-Back to the Future?
papers.abstract: Interferon (IFN) has historically played a major role in chronic viral hepatitis B and D management over the last three decades. Widening utilisation of nucleoside/nucleotide analogues (NUCs) for hepatitis B viral suppression, which have a better side-effect profile, alongside the recent licensing of bulevirtide for treatment of hepatitis D, means that its clinical use has further declined. Pegylated-interferon alpha (peg-IFNα) treatment is suboptimal with poor tolerability and achieves durable clearance of hepatitis B and D in only a limited number of patients. Nevertheless, its use in hepatitis B has significantly increased the number of patients achieving hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss compared to those on NUCs alone. Evidence has shown that peg-IFNα is also associated with overall improved long-term clinical outcomes in chronic hepatitis D, even for the many whose hepatitis D viral load rebounds after discontinuation. Clinical trials have recently focused on peg-IFNα in combination with novel antiviral therapies in the goal for finite cure in hepatitis B and D. This article focuses on recent research advances, examining if peg-IFNα treatment may still play an important role in hepatitis B and D treatment.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the historical and current role of interferon-based therapy in managing hepatitis B and D. It highlights the decline in clinical use due to the availability of nucleoside/nucleotide analogues (NUCs) and bulevirtide, which offer better side-effect profiles. Pegylated-interferon alpha (peg-IFNα) is noted as suboptimal with poor tolerability and limited durable clearance rates. However, its use in hepatitis B has increased HBsAg loss compared to NUCs alone. Additionally, peg-IFNα is associated with improved long-term clinical outcomes in chronic hepatitis D, despite viral load rebounds post-treatment. The review focuses on recent research advances and the potential for peg-IFNα to still play an important role in treatment strategies.

papers.title_zh: 乙型和丁型肝炎:基于干扰素的治疗 - 用于临床试验或标准护理 - 回到未来?
papers.source_body_en: Interferon (IFN) has historically played a major role in chronic viral hepatitis B and D management over the last three decades. Widening utilisation of nucleoside/nucleotide analogues (NUCs) for hepatitis B viral suppression, which have a better side-effect profile, alongside the recent licensing of bulevirtide for treatment of hepatitis D, means that its clinical use has further declined. Pegylated-interferon alpha (peg-IFNα) treatment is suboptimal with poor tolerability and achieves durable clearance of hepatitis B and D in only a limited number of patients. Nevertheless, its use in hepatitis B has significantly increased the number of patients achieving hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss compared to those on NUCs alone. Evidence has shown that peg-IFNα is also associated with overall improved long-term clinical outcomes in chronic hepatitis D, even for the many whose hepatitis D viral load rebounds after discontinuation. Clinical trials have recently focused on peg-IFNα in combination with novel antiviral therapies in the goal for finite cure in hepatitis B and D. This article focuses on recent research advances, examining if peg-IFNα treatment may still play an important role in hepatitis B and D treatment.

papers.title: Chronic Hepatitis B in the United States: Current Landscape, Unmet Needs and Future Directions.
papers.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection represents a major public health challenge in the US, with substantial unmet needs related to timely diagnosis, treatment, monitoring and disease management. This narrative review explores the CHB landscape in the US, including gaps in patient care, the evolving therapeutic landscape, the clinical utility of serological biomarkers to improve outcomes and the experiences of people living with hepatitis B (PLWHB). Hepatitis B remains underdiagnosed and undertreated in the US, and current efforts are insufficient to meet the associated World Health Organization 2030 elimination targets. Latest guidelines from the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the Infectious Diseases Society of America, representing a North American perspective, signify a shift towards expanded treatment eligibility criteria and shared decision-making. Nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) are the current standard of care in the US, but functional cure is rarely achieved with NAs alone. Novel finite therapies targeting functional cure, such as antisense oligonucleotides, small interfering RNAs, immune modulators and combination or sequential regimens, are under investigation. Because of the unpredictable, complex nature of CHB, biomarkers such as quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen offer prognostic value for treatment decisions and could help guide individualised CHB management. PLWHB experience psychological impacts and health-related concerns, including fear of transmission and hepatitis B virus-related complications. Opportunities for improvement of CHB management include increased screening and linkage to care, development of more treatments targeting functional cure, adoption of serological biomarkers to inform treatment decisions and prioritising the lived experiences and preferences of PLWHB.

analysis.summary_en: This review highlights the significant public health challenge posed by chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in the United States, emphasizing the need for improved diagnosis, treatment, and disease management. The review outlines the current landscape of CHB, noting that it remains underdiagnosed and undertreated, with insufficient progress towards meeting WHO 2030 elimination targets. It discusses the limitations of nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) in achieving a functional cure and highlights the potential of novel therapies and serological biomarkers to improve outcomes. The review also underscores the importance of incorporating the lived experiences and preferences of people living with hepatitis B (PLWHB) into management strategies. These findings suggest a need for expanded treatment eligibility, shared decision-making, and further research into more effective therapeutic approaches.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 感染是美国的一项重大公共卫生挑战,与及时 诊断、治疗、监测和疾病管理相关的大量需求未得到满足。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这篇叙述性综述探讨了美国慢性乙型肝炎的情况,包括患者护理方面的差距、不断发展的治疗前景、血清学生物标志物在改善乙型肝炎患者 (PLWHB) 患者的治疗结果和经历方面的临床效用。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在美国,乙型肝炎的诊断和治疗仍然不足,目前的努力不足以实现世界卫生组织相关的 2030 年消除目标。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 改善 CHB 管理的机会包括增加筛查和与护理的联系、开发更多针对 功能性治愈 的 治疗、采用血清学生物标志物来告知 治疗 决策以及优先考虑 PLWHB 的生活经历和偏好。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 由于慢性乙型肝炎的不可预测性和复杂性,定量乙型肝炎表面抗原等生物标志物可为 治疗 决策提供预后价值,并有助于指导个体化慢性乙型肝炎管理。

papers.title: Evaluating Bepirovirsen: a first-in-class treatment option for chronic hepatitis B.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Over the last decade, the therapeutic paradigm of Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) has progressively shifted from lifelong viral suppression toward the ambitious goal of a functional cure, defined by sustained HBsAg clearance with durable control of viral replication after treatment discontinuation. Bepirovirsen, an antisense oligonucleotide directed against all HBV messenger RNAs, represents one of the most promising agents for functional cure. The phase 3 B-Well reported functional cure rates approaching 20%, rising to 27% in patients with lower baseline HBsAg levels. AREA COVERED: In this review, we summarize the biological rationale, clinical evidence, and future perspectives of bepirovirsen, highlighting how emerging finite duration therapies could redefine treatment endpoints and move the field beyond viral suppression toward a realistic prospect of functional cure for patients living with CHB. EXPERT OPINION: the therapeutic landscape of CHB is shifting from lifelong viral suppression toward functional cure as a realistic and clinically meaningful endpoint. Bepirovirsen may reduce the need for indefinite treatment and monitoring, lower healthcare costs, improve patients' quality of life, and decrease the social and psychological burden associated with chronic HBV infection.

papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Over the last decade, the therapeutic paradigm of Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) has progressively shifted from lifelong viral suppression toward the ambitious goal of a functional cure, defined by sustained HBsAg clearance with durable control of viral replication after treatment discontinuation. Bepirovirsen, an antisense oligonucleotide directed against all HBV messenger RNAs, represents one of the most promising agents for functional cure. The phase 3 B-Well reported functional cure rates approaching 20%, rising to 27% in patients with lower baseline HBsAg levels. AREA COVERED: In this review, we summarize the biological rationale, clinical evidence, and future perspectives of bepirovirsen, highlighting how emerging finite duration therapies could redefine treatment endpoints and move the field beyond viral suppression toward a realistic prospect of functional cure for patients living with CHB. EXPERT OPINION: the therapeutic landscape of CHB is shifting from lifelong viral suppression toward functional cure as a realistic and clinically meaningful endpoint. Bepirovirsen may reduce the need for indefinite treatment and monitoring, lower healthcare costs, improve patients' quality of life, and decrease the social and psychological burden associated with chronic HBV infection.

papers.title: Pharmacotherapy options for managing hepatitis B in children: an update.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Children with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) may face decades of infection before developing advanced liver disease. Pediatric management remains challenging because of age-dependent treatment eligibility, limited long-term evidence, and uncertainty regarding functional cure. AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines treatment indications, international guidelines, and the efficacy and safety of interferon-based therapy and nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) in children and adolescents. International guidelines were prioritized, supplemented by PubMed and Cochrane Library searches through September 2026 without a lower publication-date limit. We discuss treatment withdrawal, developmental safety, immunosuppression, special populations and transition to adult care. Emerging therapies are assessed with particular attention to the limits of applying adult results to children. EXPERT OPINION: In our view, earlier treatment deserves further studies, but younger age alone is insufficient grounds for intervention. Favorable responses in selected childhood cohorts do not establish benefits from treating all children with high viremia. Bepirovirsen offers potential for finite therapy by reducing HBV transcripts, yet adult efficacy cannot establish pediatric benefit. Over the next five years, adolescent trials should assess sustained HBsAg loss after treatment withdrawal and acceptable safety. Until then, effective NA suppression remains a clinically valuable option, even when cure is not achieved.

papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Children with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) may face decades of infection before developing advanced liver disease. Pediatric management remains challenging because of age-dependent treatment eligibility, limited long-term evidence, and uncertainty regarding functional cure. AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines treatment indications, international guidelines, and the efficacy and safety of interferon-based therapy and nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) in children and adolescents. International guidelines were prioritized, supplemented by PubMed and Cochrane Library searches through September 2026 without a lower publication-date limit. We discuss treatment withdrawal, developmental safety, immunosuppression, special populations and transition to adult care. Emerging therapies are assessed with particular attention to the limits of applying adult results to children. EXPERT OPINION: In our view, earlier treatment deserves further studies, but younger age alone is insufficient grounds for intervention. Favorable responses in selected childhood cohorts do not establish benefits from treating all children with high viremia. Bepirovirsen offers potential for finite therapy by reducing HBV transcripts, yet adult efficacy cannot establish pediatric benefit. Over the next five years, adolescent trials should assess sustained HBsAg loss after treatment withdrawal and acceptable safety. Until then, effective NA suppression remains a clinically valuable option, even when cure is not achieved.
papers.abstract_zh: 简介:患有 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 的儿童在发展为晚期肝病之前可能会面临数十年的感染。由于年龄相关的 治疗 资格、有限的长期证据以及 功能性治愈 的不确定性,儿科管理仍然具有挑战性。涵盖领域:这篇叙述性综述探讨了 治疗 的适应症、国际指南以及基于干扰素的治疗和核苷(酸)类似物 (NA) 在儿童和青少年中的疗效和安全性。国际指南被优先考虑,并通过 2026 年 9 月之前的 PubMed 和 Cochrane 图书馆检索进行补充,没有较低的出版日期限制。我们讨论 治疗 戒断、发育安全、免疫抑制、特殊人群和向成人护理的过渡。评估新兴疗法时特别注意将成人结果应用于儿童的局限性。专家意见:我们认为,早期的治疗值得进一步研究,但仅凭年龄较小不足以进行干预。选定的儿童 队列研究 中的良好反应并不能证明治疗所有高病毒血症儿童都有益。贝匹罗韦森通过减少 HBV 转录本提供了有限治疗的潜力,但成人疗效无法确定儿科获益。在接下来的五年中,青少年试验应评估 治疗 停药后 HBsAg 持续消失以及可接受的安全性。在此之前,即使无法治愈,有效的 NA 抑制仍然是一种具有临床价值的选择。

papers.title: Host restriction networks governing hepatitis B virus cccDNA transcription and HBx-mediated counteraction.
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) is the transcriptional template sustaining viral persistence in chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Persisting in infected hepatocyte nuclei as a stable minichromosome, cccDNA evades host immune clearance and current antivirals, remaining a central obstacle to a functional cure. Recent progress has clarified the regulatory mechanisms governing cccDNA transcription. Host cells are not passive viral replication factories; they coordinate host restriction factors (HRFs) that suppress cccDNA transcription at multiple levels, including nuclear compartmentalization, epigenetic modification, promoter-level control, interferon-induced effector responses, and early cccDNA chromatin assembly. In parallel, HBV has co-evolved countermeasures that relieve these restrictions and maintain viral transcription, mainly through HBx, which hijacks host ubiquitination and chromatin-regulatory systems. Notably, as new evidence emerges on Smc5/6-mediated restriction, HBx counteraction pathways, and the cccDNA "nucleosome switch", the functional identity of molecules previously classified as restriction factors, such as Spindlin1, is being reassessed. These findings indicate that the regulatory network controlling cccDNA transcription is not a static collection of factors, but a hierarchical, dynamic, and sometimes controversial host-virus contest. This review focuses on multilayered HRF-mediated suppression of cccDNA transcription and corresponding viral countermeasures. We summarize mechanisms, recent advances, and unresolved controversies surrounding key restriction factors, and discuss their translational potential amid emerging host-targeted interventions, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for functional cure strategies for CHB based on sustained cccDNA silencing or elimination.

Notably, as new evidence emerges on Smc5/6-mediated restriction, HBx counteraction pathways, and the cccDNA "nucleosome switch", the functional identity of molecules previously classified as restriction factors, such as Spindlin1, is being reassessed. These findings indicate that the regulatory network controlling cccDNA transcription is not a static collection of factors, but a hierarchical, dynamic, and sometimes controversial host-virus contest. This review focuses on multilayered HRF-mediated suppression of cccDNA transcription and corresponding viral countermeasures. We summarize mechanisms, recent advances, and unresolved controversies surrounding key restriction factors, and discuss their translational potential amid emerging host-targeted interventions, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for functional cure strategies for CHB based on sustained cccDNA silencing or elimination.

papers.abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 共价闭合环状 DNA (共价闭合环状DNA) 是维持 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 中病毒持续存在的转录模板。共价闭合环状DNA 作为稳定的微型染色体持续存在于受感染的肝细胞核中,逃避了 宿主 免疫清除和当前的 抗病毒药物,仍然是 功能性治愈 的主要障碍。最近的进展阐明了 共价闭合环状DNA 转录的调控机制。宿主细胞不是被动的病毒复制工厂;它们协调 宿主 限制因子 (HRF),在多个水平上抑制 共价闭合环状DNA 转录,包括核区室化、表观遗传修饰、启动子水平控制、干扰素诱导的效应反应和早期 共价闭合环状DNA 染色质组装。与此同时,HBV 也有共同进化的对策,主要通过 HBx 来解除这些限制并维持病毒转录,HBx 劫持 宿主 泛素化和染色质调节系统。值得注意的是,随着关于 Smc5/6 介导的限制、HBx 反作用途径和 共价闭合环状DNA“核小体开关”的新证据的出现,之前被归类为限制因子的分子(例如 Spindlin1)的功能特性正在被重新评估。这些发现表明,控制 共价闭合环状DNA 转录的调控网络不是静态的因子集合,而是分层的、动态的、有时有争议的 宿主 病毒竞争。本综述重点关注 HRF 介导的 共价闭合环状DNA 转录的多层抑制以及相应的病毒对策。我们总结了围绕关键限制因素的机制、最新进展和未解决的争议,并讨论了它们在新兴的 宿主 靶向干预措施中的转化潜力,旨在为基于持续 共价闭合环状DNA 沉默或消除的 CHB 功能性治愈 策略提供理论基础。

papers.title: Barriers and facilitators along the continuum of care among people living with hepatitis B in EU/EEA, Switzerland and the UK: A scoping review
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) represents a significant global health burden, with approximately 14 million infected individuals in EU/EEA countries. The alarmingly low proportions diagnosed, linked to, engaged and retained in care underscore the necessity for further evidence on HBV care continuum dynamics, as emphasized in the new World Health Organisation guidelines for HBV. We conducted a scoping review to identify and describe research addressing modifiable barriers and facilitators related to the care continuum for people living with HBV infection in EU/EEA countries, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. We pre-specified our methods in a protocol, conducted the review in line with a methodological guide, searched six databases, selected eligible studies in duplicate, and summarized data descriptively. We included 24 studies, of which most were published after 2016 and were observational quantitative studies. The studies included about 25,000 participants from 11 countries, primarily immigrants living with HBV infection, of which 90% had chronic HBV infection. Six studies covered the perspectives of healthcare professionals. For each study, we determined which stage(s) of the continuum of care the study attended to, finding that nine provided outcome data on two or three stages of care. While 14 studies concerned linkage to care (stage 3) and ten studies retention in care (stage 5), few investigated testing (stage 1), referral (stage 2) or engagement in care (stage 4). We grouped the studies’ results according to the five care continuum stages and found that a handful of barriers consistently emerged across multiple continuum stages: systemic healthcare constraints (including resource constraints, deprioritization of HBV), provider knowledge deficiencies, and patients’ limited understanding of the condition and negative perceptions of HBV. More research is necessary and must encompass a broader spectrum of at-risk populations and income settings to better align with the epidemiological distribution of HBV burden across Europe.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review explores barriers and facilitators along the care continuum for people living with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in EU/EEA countries, Switzerland and the UK. The review highlights the significant global health burden of HBV, with approximately 14 million infected individuals in these regions. It identifies systemic healthcare constraints, provider knowledge deficiencies, and patient-related factors as consistent barriers across multiple stages of the care continuum. The review includes 24 observational quantitative studies involving about 25,000 participants, primarily immigrants with chronic HBV infection. While most studies focused on linkage to care and retention in care, fewer addressed testing, referral, or engagement in care. The findings emphasize the need for more research on a broader range of at-risk populations and income settings to better address the epidemiological distribution of HBV burden in Europe.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 我们进行了范围界定审查,以确定和描述针对欧盟/欧洲经济区国家、瑞士和英国乙型肝炎病毒感染者连续护理相关的可改变障碍和促进因素的研究。我们在方案中预先指定了我们的方法,根据方法指南进行了审查,检索了六个数据库,一式两份地选择了合格的研究,并对数据进行了描述性总结。

papers.title_zh: 欧盟/欧洲经济区、瑞士和英国乙型肝炎患者连续护理的障碍和促进因素:范围界定审查
papers.source_body_en: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) represents a significant global health burden, with approximately 14 million infected individuals in EU/EEA countries. The alarmingly low proportions diagnosed, linked to, engaged and retained in care underscore the necessity for further evidence on HBV care continuum dynamics, as emphasized in the new World Health Organisation guidelines for HBV. We conducted a scoping review to identify and describe research addressing modifiable barriers and facilitators related to the care continuum for people living with HBV infection in EU/EEA countries, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. We pre-specified our methods in a protocol, conducted the review in line with a methodological guide, searched six databases, selected eligible studies in duplicate, and summarized data descriptively. We included 24 studies, of which most were published after 2016 and were observational quantitative studies. The studies included about 25,000 participants from 11 countries, primarily immigrants living with HBV infection, of which 90% had chronic HBV infection. Six studies covered the perspectives of healthcare professionals. For each study, we determined which stage(s) of the continuum of care the study attended to, finding that nine provided outcome data on two or three stages of care. While 14 studies concerned linkage to care (stage 3) and ten studies retention in care (stage 5), few investigated testing (stage 1), referral (stage 2) or engagement in care (stage 4). We grouped the studies’ results according to the five care continuum stages and found that a handful of barriers consistently emerged across multiple continuum stages: systemic healthcare constraints (including resource constraints, deprioritization of HBV), provider knowledge deficiencies, and patients’ limited understanding of the condition and negative perceptions of HBV. More research is necessary and must encompass a broader spectrum of at-risk populations and income settings to better align with the epidemiological distribution of HBV burden across Europe.

papers.title: Sensorimotor Axonal Polyneuropathy Revealing Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection in the Postpartum Period: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
papers.abstract: Extrahepatic manifestations of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection are well described; however, peripheral nervous system involvement is a rare and probably underdiagnosed manifestation. We report a case of sensorimotor axonal polyneuropathy that led to the diagnosis of a previously unrecognized chronic HBV infection during the postpartum period. A 32-year-old woman, gravida 2 para 2, who delivered vaginally at home in the context of preeclampsia, developed partial functional impairment of both lower limbs during the postpartum period, accompanied by a static-kinetic cerebellar syndrome, bilateral horizontal nystagmus, and a peripheral neurogenic syndrome involving all four limbs, without digestive symptoms or clinical signs of liver disease. Workup revealed a positive hepatitis B surface antigen, positive total anti-HBc antibodies, negative HBe antigen, and an elevated HBV viral load, despite normal liver function tests. Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) serology were negative. Complement levels, cryoglobulinemia testing, and nerve/muscle biopsy were not performed. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis was normal, with no evidence of albuminocytologic dissociation. Vitamin B1 deficiency was identified, whereas vitamin B12 levels were normal and cold agglutinins were negative. Brain CT angiography and MRI were normal. Nerve conduction studies were consistent with sensorimotor axonal polyneuropathy, predominantly affecting the lower limbs. Antiviral therapy with tenofovir was initiated, and clinical and paraclinical follow-up was planned. This presentation falls within the spectrum of extrahepatic neurological manifestations of HBV infection. The associated vitamin B1 deficiency represents an important confounding factor that must be considered in the diagnostic reasoning, together with the immunological particularities of the postpartum period. The treatment decision was guided by current international recommendations regarding early antiviral therapy for HBV infection in the presence of symptomatic extrahepatic manifestations. In patients presenting with unexplained peripheral neuropathy, particularly in a suggestive clinical context, screening for chronic HBV infection should be systematic, even in the absence of hepatic abnormalities. Nevertheless, a comprehensive etiological workup is essential to exclude relevant differential diagnoses before HBV infection is considered the sole underlying cause.

papers.abstract_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒 (HBV) 感染的肝外表现已有详细描述;然而,周围神经系统受累是一种罕见且可能未被充分诊断的表现。我们报告了一例感觉运动轴突多发性神经病,该病导致产后期间先前未被识别的慢性 HBV 感染 诊断。一名32岁女性,2月2日妊娠,因先兆子痫在家中阴道分娩,产后出现双下肢部分功能障碍,伴有静动小脑综合征、双侧水平眼球震颤和累及四肢的周围神经源性综合征,无消化道症状或肝病临床体征。尽管肝功能检查正常,但检查显示乙型肝炎表面抗原阳性、总抗 HBc 抗体阳性、HBe 抗原阴性以及 HBV 病毒载量升高。抗中性粒细胞胞浆抗体(ANCA)和丙型肝炎病毒(HCV)血清学 均为阴性。未进行补体水平、冷球蛋白血症检测和神经/肌肉活检。脑脊液(CSF)分析正常,没有白蛋白细胞解离的证据。发现维生素 B1 缺乏,而维生素 B12 水平正常,冷凝集素呈阴性。脑CT血管造影和MRI均正常。神经传导研究与感觉运动轴突多发性神经病一致,主要影响下肢。开始使用替诺福韦进行 抗病毒药物 治疗,并计划进行临床和临床旁随访。这种表现属于乙型肝炎病毒感染的肝外神经系统表现范围。相关的维生素 B1 缺乏是一个重要的混杂因素,在诊断推理中必须考虑该因素以及产后期的免疫学特殊性。治疗 决定以当前国际建议为指导,该建议涉及在存在症状性肝外表现的情况下对 HBV 感染进行早期 抗病毒药物 治疗。对于出现不明原因周围神经病变的患者,特别是在提示性临床背景下,即使没有肝脏异常,也应该系统地筛查慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染。然而,在乙型肝炎病毒感染被认为是唯一的根本原因之前,全面的病因学检查对于排除相关的鉴别诊断至关重要。

papers.title: Comparative Analysis Reveals Distinct Host Extrachromosomal Circular DNA Profiles Across HBV Infection and HBV-Associated Models of Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Extrachromosomal circular DNAs (eccDNAs) range from small microDNAs and small polydispersed circular DNAs to megabase‐scale extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA). Although ecDNA has been implicated in virus‐associated cancers, how oncogenic viruses influence the broader host eccDNA landscape remains poorly understood. Here, we characterized eccDNA in primary human hepatocytes (PHHs) infected with wild‐type hepatitis B virus (HBV) or an HBV mutant lacking the regulatory X protein (HBVΔX) and compared these profiles with those of the HBV‐associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cell lines Hep3B and PLC/PRF/5. Using genome‐wide sequencing, computational analyses, and targeted experimental validation, we applied a gene‐centric framework to identify loci recurrently represented on eccDNA and prioritized candidates relevant to HBV‐associated hepatocarcinogenesis. We observed a heterogeneous eccDNA landscape that included a subset of recurrent gene‐associated loci detected during acute HBV infection and altered expression of selected candidates in HBV‐HCC models. These findings establish a framework for integrating eccDNA profiles across acute infection and transformed cellular contexts. More broadly, they support further investigation of eccDNAs as potential molecular records of virus‐associated genomic stress and as candidate contributors to HBV‐associated disease progression.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how oncogenic viruses influence the broader host extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) landscape, particularly in the context of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study characterized eccDNA in primary human hepatocytes (PHHs) infected with wild-type HBV or an HBV mutant lacking the regulatory X protein (HBVΔX) and compared these profiles with those of HBV-associated HCC cell lines Hep3B and PLC/PRF/5.
analysis.methods: The researchers used genome-wide sequencing, computational analyses, and targeted experimental validation to apply a gene-centric framework for identifying loci recurrently represented on eccDNA and prioritizing candidates relevant to HBV-associated hepatocarcinogenesis.
analysis.main_results: A heterogeneous eccDNA landscape was observed, including a subset of recurrent gene-associated loci detected during acute HBV infection and altered expression of selected candidates in HBV-HCC models.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish a framework for integrating eccDNA profiles across acute infection and transformed cellular contexts, highlighting the potential role of eccDNAs in virus-associated genomic stress and disease progression.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying HBV-associated disease progression and suggest the utility of eccDNA profiling for understanding and monitoring virus-induced genomic changes in hepatocellular carcinoma.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on specific HBV infection models and cell lines, which may not fully represent the complexity of human HBV infection. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the controlled experimental setting.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) profiles in primary human hepatocytes infected with hepatitis B virus (HBV) and HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) models. Using genome-wide sequencing and computational analyses, the researchers identified recurrent gene-associated loci and altered expression patterns in these contexts. The findings suggest that eccDNA may serve as a molecular record of HBV-induced genomic stress and contribute to disease progression. The study provides a framework for integrating eccDNA profiles across different stages of HBV infection and HCC. However, the results are based on controlled experimental models, which may limit their generalizability to broader human populations. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the specific focus on these models.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查致癌病毒如何影响更广泛的 宿主 染色体外环状 DNA (eccDNA) 景观,特别是在 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染和 HBV 相关肝细胞癌 (HCC) 的背景下。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究对感染野生型 HBV 或缺乏调节性 X 蛋白 (HBVΔX) 的 HBV 突变体 (HBVΔX) 的原代人肝细胞 (PHH) 中的 eccDNA 进行了表征,并将这些图谱与 HBV 相关 HCC 细胞系 Hep3B 和 PLC/PRF/5 的图谱进行了比较。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用 基因组 全测序、计算分析和有针对性的实验验证,应用以基因为中心的框架来识别 eccDNA 上经常出现的基因座,并优先考虑与 HBV 相关肝癌发生相关的候选基因。
elements_zh.main_results: 观察到异质 eccDNA 景观,包括急性 HBV 感染期间检测到的复发基因相关位点子集以及 HBV-HCC 模型中选定候选者的表达改变。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果建立了一个框架,用于整合急性感染和转化细胞环境中的 eccDNA 图谱,强调了 eccDNA 在病毒相关基因组应激和疾病进展中的潜在作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对 HBV 相关疾病进展的分子机制的见解,并表明 eccDNA 分析可用于理解和监测病毒诱导的肝细胞癌基因组变化。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其重点关注特定的乙型肝炎病毒感染模型和细胞系,可能无法完全代表人类乙型肝炎病毒感染的复杂性。由于受控的实验设置,证据的强度适中。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 染色体外环状 DNA (eccDNA) 范围从小型 microDNA 和小型多分散环状 DNA 到兆碱基规模的染色体外 DNA (ecDNA)。尽管 ecDNA 与病毒相关癌症有关,但致癌病毒如何影响更广泛的 宿主 eccDNA 景观仍然知之甚少。在这里,我们对感染野生型 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 或缺乏调节性 X 蛋白 (HBVΔX) 的 HBV 突变体 (HBVΔX) 的原代人肝细胞 (PHH) 中的 eccDNA 进行了表征,并将这些图谱与 HBV 相关肝细胞癌 (HCC) 细胞系 Hep3B 和 PLC/PRF/5 的图谱进行了比较。使用 基因组 全范围测序、计算分析和有针对性的实验验证,我们应用以基因为中心的框架来识别 eccDNA 上经常出现的基因座,并优先考虑与 HBV 相关肝癌发生相关的候选基因。我们观察到异质 eccDNA 景观,其中包括急性 HBV 感染期间检测到的复发基因相关基因座的子集以及 HBV-HCC 模型中选定候选者的表达改变。这些发现建立了一个框架,用于整合急性感染和转化细胞环境中的 eccDNA 图谱。更广泛地说,他们支持进一步研究 eccDNA 作为病毒相关基因组应激的潜在分子记录和 HBV 相关疾病进展的候选贡献者。

papers.title: Immunogenicity of titer guided intensified hepatitis B vaccination strategy in children with cancer.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To assess the immunogenicity of a titer-guided, intensified hepatitis B vaccination protocol in children with malignancies receiving chemotherapy. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included children aged 100 mIU/mL received no additional vaccination. Follow-up anti-HBs titers were assessed to evaluate immune response. RESULTS: Among 169 children, follow-up anti-HBs titers were available for 135. At baseline, 79 (46.7%) children had anti-HBs 100 mIU/mL. Among 94 vaccinated children, 47 (50.0%) achieved a robust serological response (> 100 mIU/mL). Robust responses were more frequent in those with baseline anti-HBs titers of 10-100 mIU/mL. Response rates were higher in younger children, but the difference was not statistically significant. CONCLUSION: A titer-guided intensified hepatitis B vaccination strategy was associated with robust serological response, particularly in children with partial pre-existing immunity.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the immunogenicity of a titer-guided, intensified hepatitis B vaccination strategy in children with cancer receiving chemotherapy. The retrospective cohort design included 169 children, with follow-up anti-HBs titers assessed to evaluate immune response. Among the 135 children with available titers, 79 (46.7%) had baseline anti-HBs titers of 100 mIU/mL, and 47 (50.0%) of the 94 vaccinated children achieved a robust serological response (> 100 mIU/mL). The authors interpreted these results as evidence that the titer-guided strategy was associated with improved serological response, especially in children with partial pre-existing immunity. The study's findings have implications for optimizing hepatitis B vaccination protocols in immunocompromised pediatric populations. However, the retrospective nature of the study and potential biases in data collection limit the confidence in the results, though the evidence is considered strong due to the direct association observed between vaccination strategy and immune response.

papers.title: HCC risk in HBeAg-positive chronic hepatitis B: impact of low baseline HBsAg and poor on-treatment decline.
papers.abstract: AIM: The association between hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development during long-term nucleos(t)ide analog (NUC) treatment remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between quantitative HBsAg (qHBsAg) levels and HCC incidence in patients with baseline HBeAg positivity who were receiving NUC treatment. METHODS: Overall, 951 patients with chronic hepatitis B with baseline HBeAg positivity who had received NUC treatment for at least 1 year were included. The outcomes evaluated were HCC incidence and HBsAg loss (< 0.05 IU/mL) according to baseline and on-treatment HBsAg kinetics. RESULTS: Over a 14.7-year median treatment duration, 98 patients developed HCC. A low baseline qHBsAg level (< 10,000 IU/mL) was significantly associated with a three to four times higher risk of HCC than a high baseline qHBsAg level (≥ 10,000 IU/mL). Baseline HBV DNA levels also showed the association with HCC in univariate analysis as previously reported. qHBsAg was superior to HBV DNA for predicting the risk of HCC in multivariable analysis and receiver operating characteristic curves analysis. Furthermore, patients with low baseline qHBsAg levels and low decline in qHBsAg levels during the first year of treatment independently had a high risk of HCC. Conversely, the HBsAg seroclearance rates were lower in patients with low baseline qHBsAg levels and low decline in qHBsAg levels. CONCLUSIONS: Low baseline qHBsAg levels and poor decline in qHBsAg were associated with a high risk of HCC, and the rarity of HBsAg loss in patients with baseline HBeAg positivity who were receiving NUC treatment.

This study aimed to investigate the association between quantitative HBsAg (qHBsAg) levels and HCC incidence in patients with baseline HBeAg positivity who were receiving NUC treatment. METHODS: Overall, 951 patients with chronic hepatitis B with baseline HBeAg positivity who had received NUC treatment for at least 1 year were included. The outcomes evaluated were HCC incidence and HBsAg loss (< 0.05 IU/mL) according to baseline and on-treatment HBsAg kinetics. RESULTS: Over a 14.7-year median treatment duration, 98 patients developed HCC. A low baseline qHBsAg level (< 10,000 IU/mL) was significantly associated with a three to four times higher risk of HCC than a high baseline qHBsAg level (≥ 10,000 IU/mL). Baseline HBV DNA levels also showed the association with HCC in univariate analysis as previously reported. qHBsAg was superior to HBV DNA for predicting the risk of HCC in multivariable analysis and receiver operating characteristic curves analysis. Furthermore, patients with low baseline qHBsAg levels and low decline in qHBsAg levels during the first year of treatment independently had a high risk of HCC. Conversely, the HBsAg seroclearance rates were lower in patients with low baseline qHBsAg levels and low decline in qHBsAg levels. CONCLUSIONS: Low baseline qHBsAg levels and poor decline in qHBsAg were associated with a high risk of HCC, and the rarity of HBsAg loss in patients with baseline HBeAg positivity who were receiving NUC treatment.

papers.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver and antiviral response in chronic hepatitis B: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) frequently coexists with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). However, its association with antiviral treatment responses and long-term clinical outcomes in patients with CHB remains unclear. AIM To systematically evaluate the impact of MAFLD on antiviral treatment responses and long-term clinical outcomes in patients with CHB. METHODS This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed, the Cochrane Library, EMBASE, and Web of Science were searched for studies published up to November 30, 2025. Meta-analyses were performed to assess associations between MAFLD and antiviral treatment responses or clinical outcomes. Subgroup analyses were conducted according to antiviral regimen and MAFLD diagnostic approach, and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate robustness. RESULTS Thirty-two studies were included, of which 20 evaluated antiviral treatment efficacy and 13 assessed clinical outcomes in patients with CHB and concomitant MAFLD (one study reported both treatment responses and clinical outcomes). MAFLD was associated with a higher rate of hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance at 48 weeks [odds ratio (OR) = 1.41, 95%CI: 1.28-1.55], although this association was attenuated at 96 weeks (OR = 1.44, 95%CI: 0.96-2.16). No significant association was observed between MAFLD and hepatitis B e antigen seroclearance at any time-point. MAFLD was consistently associated with lower rates of alanine aminotransferase normalization and hepatitis B virus DNA clearance throughout the treatment duration. MAFLD was associated with a significantly increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) despite antiviral therapy (OR = 1.50, 95%CI: 1.01-2.24). Subgroup analyses according to the antiviral regimen revealed distinct patterns, partly explaining the heterogeneity in the overall analyses. Subgroup analyses suggested that the antiviral regimen and MAFLD diagnostic approach partly explained the heterogeneity, particularly for hepatitis B virus DNA clearance and HCC. CONCLUSION MAFLD was associated with lower virological and biochemical response rates, higher odds of hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance at week 48, particularly among patients receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy, and higher odds of HCC in patients with CHB, but not with hepatitis B e antigen seroclearance. These findings support metabolic risk assessment in CHB management and highlight the need for standardized MAFLD/metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease definitions.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本系统评价和荟萃分析遵循系统评价和荟萃分析的首选报告项目 (PRISMA) 指南。对 PubMed、Cochrane 图书馆、EMBASE 和 Web of Science 检索了截至 2025 年 11 月 30 日发表的研究。进行荟萃分析以评估 MAFLD 和 抗病毒药物 治疗 反应或临床结果之间的关联。根据抗病毒药物方案和MAFLD诊断方法进行亚组分析,并进行留一敏感性分析以评估稳健性。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: MAFLD 与较低的病毒学和生化反应率、第 48 周时乙型肝炎表面抗原血清清除的几率较高(特别是在接受核苷(酸)类似物治疗的患者中)以及 CHB 患者发生肝细胞癌(HCC)的几率较高相关。在任何时间点均未观察到 MAFLD 与乙型肝炎 e 抗原血清清除之间存在显着关联。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 亚组分析表明,抗病毒药物 方案和 MAFLD 诊断方法部分解释了异质性,特别是对于 乙型肝炎病毒 DNA 清除率和 HCC。MAFLD 和 抗病毒药物 治疗 反应之间的关联在 96 周时减弱。

papers.title: Anti-Viral Treatment Eligibility and Treatment Uptake Among People With Chronic Hepatitis B in Australia: The REACH-B Study.
papers.abstract: Treatment indication for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) varies across clinical guidelines. This study evaluated treatment eligibility and uptake in a large Australian cohort of people with CHB. The REACH-B study recruited people with CHB managed through a national network of healthcare services. Participants were categorised into three groups: (1) receiving antiviral therapy; (2) untreated despite eligibility; (3) untreated and ineligible. Treatment eligibility was determined using Australian Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) criteria, and by international clinical guidelines. Among 3648 participants (56% male; median age 48 years; 49% born in North-East or South-East Asia; 27% First Nations Australians), 14% were HBeAg positive and 7% had cirrhosis. Overall, 47% (n = 1666) were on antiviral therapy, 45% (n = 1573) were untreated and ineligible and 7% (n = 251) were untreated despite eligibility based on Australian PBS criteria. In adjusted analysis, the likelihood of remaining untreated despite eligibility was higher among women (aOR 1.59, 95% CI 1.34, 1.88) and younger participants (age 41-60 vs. > 60 years: aOR 1.51, 95% CI 1.01-2.28; ≤ 40 vs. > 60 years: aOR 2.65, 95% CI 1.60, 4.40). The proportion untreated despite eligibility increased to 13% when applying 2024 World Health Organisation guidelines and ranged 2%-44% based on other guidelines, highlighting the variability across the guidelines. In conclusion, among REACH-B participants, most eligible individuals receive treatment. Lower treatment uptake among women and younger people despite eligibility partly reflects lower threshold for elevated ALT in women, and clinician determination of non-CHB related ALT elevation. As treatment guidelines evolve and eligibility criteria broaden, monitoring treatment patterns is important.

papers.title: Comparative risk of hepatocellular carcinoma among people with chronic hepatitis B treated with tenofovir or entecavir: A population-based linkage study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) incidence and mortality are rising in Australia and globally. Antiviral therapies entecavir (ETV) and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) are widely used to treat chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and reduce HCC risk, but uncertainty persists regarding their relative HCC prevention impact. This study characterises HCC incidence among people with CHB treated with ETV or TDF, including sub-populations recommended for HCC surveillance. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study in New South Wales, Australia, using linked public health datasets: 10,698 people with CHB were eligible after receiving at least 12 months of stable antiviral therapy with ETV (n=7,139) or TDF (n=3,559). Follow-up occurred from 2007-2022. Crude annual incidence rates and adjusted Cox proportional hazard ratios were calculated for HCC. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 86.3 months, including 89.2 months and 82.3 months among participants receiving TDF and ETV, respectively. During follow-up, 300 (2.8%) participants were diagnosed with HCC, an incidence of 4.12 per 1000 person years. Participants treated with TDF had a lower hazard ratio for HCC (aHR: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.46-0.82) compared to those treated with ETV. Baseline variables associated with increased HCC risk were older age (reference <50 years: 50-59 years aHR: 2.15, 95% CI: 1.45-3.18; 60-69 years aHR: 3.42, 95% CI: 2.38-4.91; 70-79 years aHR: 4.28, 95% CI: 2.89-6.34; ≥80 years aHR: 3.95, 95% CI: 2.51-6.22), male sex (aHR: 3.14; 95% CI: 2.31-4.25), alcohol use disorder (aHR: 2.33; 95% CI: 1.28-4.25), and history of decompensated cirrhosis (aHR: 2.28; 95% CI: 1.27-4.07). CONCLUSION: In people with chronic hepatitis B in Australia on stable antiviral therapy hepatocellular carcinoma risk was lower among those receiving entecavir than those receiving tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, although confounding remains a potential explanation. IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: Comparative HCC risk between entecavir and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) in chronic hepatitis B remains uncertain outside East Asian cohorts. This population-based linkage study of people with chronic hepatitis B in Australia found TDF was associated with lower HCC risk than entecavir, a finding relevant to clinicians and researchers working on HCC prevention. These results support consideration of TDF as a preferred antiviral where clinically appropriate and highlight the need for HCC screening guidelines to account for treatment status alongside established risk factors such as older age and alcohol use disorder. As treatment was not randomised and residual confounding could not be completely mitigated, further prospective studies are needed to confirm this association.

papers.title: Discordant serology and nucleic acid testing results in blood donor screening: Causes, resolution pathways and operational implications-A narrative review.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Combined serological and nucleic acid testing (NAT) has narrowed the infectious window period for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV), yet the two still disagree on a small fraction of donations. This narrative review aimed to identify the causes of serology-NAT discordance, describe the laboratory approaches used to investigate it, highlight heterogeneous practice and propose evidence-graded resolution pathways. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE literature published between January 2000 and August 2026 was reviewed with US, European, UK, World Health Organization (WHO) and International Society of Blood Transfusion (ISBT) regulatory and professional guidance. Causes of discordance were classified as temporal marker discordance, biological discordance, analytical false reactivity, analytical false negativity or pre-analytical error and mapped by virus and, for HBV, by reactive marker to investigation and donor-management steps. RESULTS: Serology-reactive/NAT-nonreactive results usually reflect analytical false reactivity or resolved infection. HBV is the main exception: the meaning depends on whether hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), total antibody to hepatitis B core antigen (anti-HBc) or immunoglobulin M (IgM) anti-HBc is reactive, and low-level or intermittent viraemia may escape minipool NAT. NAT-reactive/serology-nonreactive results mostly represent window-period infection, and their interpretation depends on NAT format, discriminatory testing, repeatability and access to confirmatory testing. Donor re-entry rules differ substantially between jurisdictions. CONCLUSION: We provide general and virus-specific algorithms, with HBV structured by reactive marker, in which each step is labelled as a regulatory requirement, professional guidance, common practice or the authors' proposal. Establishments can adapt these pathways to local regulation and confirmatory capacity to reduce missed infections and unnecessary donor loss.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, examining the causes of discordance between serology and nucleic acid testing (NAT) in blood donor screening. The central question is to identify the reasons for such discordance, describe laboratory approaches to investigate it, highlight heterogeneous practices, and propose resolution pathways.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of PubMed/MEDLINE literature published between January 2000 and August 2026, incorporating US, European, UK, World Health Organization (WHO), and International Society of Blood Transfusion (ISBT) regulatory and professional guidance. The evidence is classified into categories such as temporal marker discordance, biological discordance, analytical false reactivity, analytical false negativity, and pre-analytical error.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Serology-reactive/NAT-nonreactive results typically indicate analytical false reactivity or resolved infection. HBV is an exception, where the interpretation depends on the reactive marker (HBsAg, anti-HBc, or IgM anti-HBc) and the possibility of low-level or intermittent viraemia escaping minipool NAT. NAT-reactive/serology-nonreactive results are mostly due to window-period infections, and their interpretation depends on NAT format, discriminatory testing, repeatability, and access to confirmatory testing. Donor re-entry rules vary significantly across jurisdictions.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is heterogeneity in practices and interpretations across different jurisdictions. The review highlights that HBV-related discordance is complex and depends on the reactive marker, with limited evidence on the frequency of low-level viraemia. Additionally, the interpretation of NAT-reactive/serology-nonreactive results is influenced by factors such as NAT format and confirmatory testing availability, which may not be uniformly applied.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that blood establishments should adapt resolution pathways to local regulations and confirmatory testing capacities to reduce missed infections and unnecessary donor loss. Further research is needed to better understand HBV-specific discordance mechanisms and to standardize practices across jurisdictions.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review explores the causes of discordance between serology and nucleic acid testing (NAT) in blood donor screening for hepatitis B virus (HBV). It identifies key factors such as analytical false reactivity, resolved infection, and low-level viraemia as potential explanations for discordant results. The review emphasizes the importance of considering reactive markers and NAT formats in interpretation, while highlighting jurisdictional differences in donor re-entry rules. It proposes virus-specific algorithms for resolving discordance and underscores the need for tailored approaches based on local regulations and confirmatory testing capabilities. The review also points to gaps in understanding HBV-specific discordance and the need for further research to standardize practices.

papers.title_zh: 献血者筛查中不一致的 血清学 和核酸检测结果:原因、解决途径和操作影响 - 叙述性回顾。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Combined serological and nucleic acid testing (NAT) has narrowed the infectious window period for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV), yet the two still disagree on a small fraction of donations. This narrative review aimed to identify the causes of serology-NAT discordance, describe the laboratory approaches used to investigate it, highlight heterogeneous practice and propose evidence-graded resolution pathways. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE literature published between January 2000 and August 2026 was reviewed with US, European, UK, World Health Organization (WHO) and International Society of Blood Transfusion (ISBT) regulatory and professional guidance. Causes of discordance were classified as temporal marker discordance, biological discordance, analytical false reactivity, analytical false negativity or pre-analytical error and mapped by virus and, for HBV, by reactive marker to investigation and donor-management steps. RESULTS: Serology-reactive/NAT-nonreactive results usually reflect analytical false reactivity or resolved infection. HBV is the main exception: the meaning depends on whether hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), total antibody to hepatitis B core antigen (anti-HBc) or immunoglobulin M (IgM) anti-HBc is reactive, and low-level or intermittent viraemia may escape minipool NAT. NAT-reactive/serology-nonreactive results mostly represent window-period infection, and their interpretation depends on NAT format, discriminatory testing, repeatability and access to confirmatory testing. Donor re-entry rules differ substantially between jurisdictions. CONCLUSION: We provide general and virus-specific algorithms, with HBV structured by reactive marker, in which each step is labelled as a regulatory requirement, professional guidance, common practice or the authors' proposal. Establishments can adapt these pathways to local regulation and confirmatory capacity to reduce missed infections and unnecessary donor loss.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景和目的:血清学和核酸联合检测(NAT)缩小了人类免疫缺陷病毒(HIV)、乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)和丙型肝炎病毒(HCV)的传染窗口期,但两者在一小部分捐赠方面仍存在分歧。这篇叙述性综述旨在确定 血清学-NAT 不一致的原因,描述用于调查它的实验室方法,强调异构实践并提出证据分级的解决途径。材料和方法:在美国、欧洲、英国、世界卫生组织 (WHO) 和国际输血协会 (ISBT) 监管和专业指导下对 2000 年 1 月至 2026 年 8 月期间发表的 PubMed/MEDLINE 文献进行了审查。不一致的原因被分类为时间标记不一致、生物学不一致、分析性假反应性、分析性假阴性或分析前错误,并按病毒进行映射,对于乙型肝炎,按反应性标记进行调查和供者管理步骤。结果:血清学 反应/NAT 非反应结果通常反映分析错误反应或已解决的感染。HBV 是主要的例外:其含义取决于乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg)、乙型肝炎核心抗原总抗体 (抗 HBc) 或免疫球蛋白 M (IgM) 抗 HBc 是否具有反应性,低水平或间歇性病毒血症可能会逃避小型池 NAT。NAT 反应/血清学-非反应结果主要代表窗口期感染,其解释取决于 NAT 格式、歧视性测试、可重复性和验证性测试的获取。不同司法管辖区的捐赠者重新进入规则存在很大差异。结论:我们提供通用和病毒特异性算法,其中 HBV 是由反应性标记构建的,其中每个步骤都被标记为监管要求、专业指导、常见做法或作者建议。企业可以根据当地监管和确认能力调整这些途径,以减少漏诊和不必要的捐赠者损失。

papers.title: Hepatitis B Birth Dose Vaccination in the United States, January 2018-June 2026.
papers.abstract: AbstractOn December 5, 2025, the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices voted to replace its 1991 recommendation for universal newborn hepatitis B vaccination (HBV) at birth with vaccination based on maternal HBV status. Using a subset of Truveta Data, an electronic health record database with deterministically linked mother-child dyads that includes data on over 140 million people with geographic representation across the United States, we describe newborn HBV vaccination rates and report rates based on maternal HBV test results. From January 2018 through June 2026, we identified 1,338,961 infants born to 1,075,767 mothers; 90.5% of pregnant mothers had evidence of an HBV test, of which 0.18% were HBsAg-positive. Newborn vaccination rates were 76.4% in 2018 and a mean of 80.0% from 2020 to 2022, then began to decline in 2023, falling to 65.6% in 2026.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the impact of the updated hepatitis B vaccination policy based on maternal HBV status on newborn vaccination rates in the United States. This is important due to the changing recommendations for hepatitis B prevention.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed data from January 2018 through June 2026 using a subset of Truveta Data, which includes over 140 million people with linked mother-child dyads. It focused on infants born to mothers with HBV test results.
analysis.methods: The researchers used an electronic health record database to describe newborn HBV vaccination rates and report these rates based on maternal HBV test results, focusing on the period from January 2018 through June 2026.
analysis.main_results: Newborn vaccination rates were 76.4% in 2018 and averaged 80.0% from 2020 to 2022, but declined to 65.6% in 2026.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the decline in vaccination rates as a potential consequence of the updated policy, highlighting the need for further investigation into its implementation and effectiveness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that changes in vaccination policy may affect coverage rates, which could have implications for public health strategies aimed at preventing hepatitis B transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only data, which may limit the depth of analysis and confidence in the conclusions drawn.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the impact of the updated hepatitis B vaccination policy in the United States, which replaced universal newborn vaccination with vaccination based on maternal HBV status. Using Truveta Data, the researchers analyzed newborn HBV vaccination rates from 2018 to 2026, finding that rates declined from 80.0% in 2020-2022 to 65.6% in 2026. papers.source_body_en: AbstractOn December 5, 2025, the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices voted to replace its 1991 recommendation for universal newborn hepatitis B vaccination (HBV) at birth with vaccination based on maternal HBV status. Using a subset of Truveta Data, an electronic health record database with deterministically linked mother-child dyads that includes data on over 140 million people with geographic representation across the United States, we describe newborn HBV vaccination rates and report rates based on maternal HBV test results. From January 2018 through June 2026, we identified 1,338,961 infants born to 1,075,767 mothers; 90.5% of pregnant mothers had evidence of an HBV test, of which 0.18% were HBsAg-positive. Newborn vaccination rates were 76.4% in 2018 and a mean of 80.0% from 2020 to 2022, then began to decline in 2023, falling to 65.6% in 2026.

papers.title: Testing for hepatitis C virus and hepatitis B virus/hepatitis D virus: Current scenarios and perspectives in Italy
papers.abstract: Liver disease accounts for approximately 4% of all deaths worldwide, and viral hepatitis affects more than 300 million people. The World Health Organization aims to reduce new hepatitis infections by 90% and deaths by 65% by 2030 through vaccination and screening programs. In Italy, screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) benefits from dedicated government funding, whereas testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) is supported by recommendations from scientific societies but does not benefit from dedicated national public health programmes. This expert-opinion review summarises the experience of tertiary-level Italian centres actively engaged in hospital-based testing for HCV, HBV, and HDV and identifies practical pathways to improve testing and linkage to care. This article presents proposals to improve the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy by: (1) Strengthening coordination between hospital units and integrating information systems between general practitioners and hospitals; (2) Implementing a centralised reporting system and a structured referral network to ensure that patients with positive test results receive appropriate therapies in a timely manner; (3) Providing the resources needed to increase testing in public addiction treatment services (Servizi per le Dipendenze) and prisons; (4) Promoting screening in high-risk populations, including vulnerable and older populations; and (5) Implementing a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis. These measures could help Italy make concrete progress towards eliminating HCV infection and controlling HBV/HDV infection within the next decade.

analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This expert-opinion review summarises the experience of tertiary-level Italian centres actively engaged in hospital-based testing for HCV, HBV, and HDV and identifies practical pathways to improve testing and linkage to care.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: In Italy, screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) benefits from dedicated government funding, whereas testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) is supported by recommendations from scientific societies but does not benefit from dedicated national public health programmes.

analysis.research_and_practice_implications: This article presents proposals to improve the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy by: (1) Strengthening coordination between hospital units and integrating information systems between general practitioners and hospitals; (2) Implementing a centralised reporting system and a structured referral network to ensure that patients with positive test results receive appropriate therapies in a timely manner; (3) Providing the resources needed to increase testing in public addiction treatment services (Servizi per le Dipendenze) and prisons; (4) Promoting screening in high-risk populations, including vulnerable and older populations; and (5) Implementing a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on the current testing scenarios for hepatitis B virus (HBV) in Italy, highlighting the lack of dedicated national public health programs for HBV and hepatitis D virus (HDV) compared to hepatitis C virus (HCV). It outlines the importance of HBV in global liver disease mortality and emphasizes the need for improved coordination between hospital units and general practitioners, centralized reporting systems, and increased testing in high-risk populations. The review also proposes a national awareness campaign to enhance HBV management. The evidence is based on expert opinions from tertiary-level Italian centers, and the findings suggest that targeted interventions could help Italy achieve its goals of reducing hepatitis infections and deaths by 2030.

papers.title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒和乙型肝炎病毒/丁型肝炎病毒检测:意大利当前状况与展望
papers.source_body_en: Liver disease accounts for approximately 4% of all deaths worldwide, and viral hepatitis affects more than 300 million people. The World Health Organization aims to reduce new hepatitis infections by 90% and deaths by 65% by 2030 through vaccination and screening programs. In Italy, screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) benefits from dedicated government funding, whereas testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) is supported by recommendations from scientific societies but does not benefit from dedicated national public health programmes. This expert-opinion review summarises the experience of tertiary-level Italian centres actively engaged in hospital-based testing for HCV, HBV, and HDV and identifies practical pathways to improve testing and linkage to care. This article presents proposals to improve the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy by: (1) Strengthening coordination between hospital units and integrating information systems between general practitioners and hospitals; (2) Implementing a centralised reporting system and a structured referral network to ensure that patients with positive test results receive appropriate therapies in a timely manner; (3) Providing the resources needed to increase testing in public addiction treatment services (Servizi per le Dipendenze) and prisons; (4) Promoting screening in high-risk populations, including vulnerable and older populations; and (5) Implementing a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis. These measures could help Italy make concrete progress towards eliminating HCV infection and controlling HBV/HDV infection within the next decade.

papers.title: Infective pylephlebitis complicating chronic portal vein thrombosis in a patient with hepatitis B-related cirrhosis: a case report and review of the literature
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Infective pylephlebitis is suppurative thrombophlebitis of the portal venous system. It is rare, lethal when recognition is delayed, and almost always described in patients without pre-existing portal vein thrombosis (PVT). In cirrhosis with chronic PVT, anticoagulation is constrained by varices and coagulopathy, and no guidance covers the infected thrombus. Case presentation: A 68-year-old Han Chinese man with hepatitis B-related decompensated cirrhosis, previous variceal bleeding treated by splenectomy, and chronic PVT maintained on low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) for 5 years presented with fever, abdominal pain and back distension. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) showed occlusion of the main portal vein and superior mesenteric vein, periportal collaterals and right colonic mural oedema; blood culture grew non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae . Continuous intravenous unfractionated heparin (UFH) targeting an activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) of 50–70 s was started together with cefoperazone/sulbactam. On day 3 the patient declined the infusion pump and was changed to subcutaneous LMWH. On day 5 the pain worsened, the APTT fell to 31.3 s, the D-dimer rose from 2.07 to 18.74 mg/L and CT showed thrombus extending into the collateral vessels. Continuous UFH was resumed after multidisciplinary review. Over the next two weeks the fever and abdominal pain resolved and the diarrhoea improved; C-reactive protein fell from 20.14 to 0.79 mg/L, and the portal vein was patent on day 12 and fully patent by day 31. Ascites that had persisted for years and diarrhoea present for 5 years resolved completely. Conclusions Chronic PVT does not protect against superimposed infective pylephlebitis, and bloodstream infection can convert a stable thrombus into a propagating one within days. High fever, worsening abdominal or back pain and an abrupt rise in D-dimer should prompt immediate contrast-enhanced CT. Once the diagnosis is established, culture-directed antimicrobials combined with continuous intravenous heparinization, titrated to APTT and interrupted when bleeding risk rises, can achieve recanalization despite previous variceal haemorrhage. Clinical improvement lags behind thrombus resolution, and a high D-dimer in the first week is not a reason to stop heparin.
