Here are five stocks we like better. Precision BioSciences plans to advance PBGENE-HBV into Phase II to test whether it can eliminate enough hepatitis B cccDNA for a viral cure. The study will evaluate the treatment alone and followed by bepirovirsen, with initial Phase II data expected in the second half of 2027. Duchenne muscular dystrophy data are expected in 2027: three-month biopsy results from roughly the first three patients could arrive around the second quarter, with the first patient's 12-month biopsy data expected in the fall. The first patient had no serious adverse events reported, and the safety board supported continued dosing. After a recent $125 million raise, the company reported cash of more than $200 million and said its runway extends into the fourth quarter of 2029. Precision BioSciences (NASDAQ:DTIL) plans to advance its hepatitis B gene-editing treatment into a Phase II study and expects initial biopsy results from its Duchenne muscular dystrophy program in 2027, executives said at a Jefferies conference. Chief Scientific Officer Cassie Gorsuch said the hepatitis B study will test whether the company's treatment, PBGENE-HBV, can reduce enough of the viral material known as cccDNA to achieve a viral cure. Chief Operating Officer Alex Kelly said the company expects to begin seeing Phase II data in the second half of 2027. → Gold Is Down 35%—Is the Bull Case Broken or Just Bruised? Kelly also said Precision had $108 million in cash as of Sept. 30 and recently raised $125 million, taking its cash balance above $200 million. He said the company's cash runway extends into the fourth quarter of 2029. Hepatitis B program moves toward Phase II Gorsuch said 25 patients had received PBGENE-HBV in the repeat-dose Phase I study, with 59 administrations across the group. At a recent liver meeting, the company reported that six patients with at least six months of follow-up after their pregenomic RNA, or pgRNA, became undetectable continued to have undetectable levels. → Plug Power Near $1: A Hydrogen Turnaround or Another False Start? The company views pgRNA as a primary biomarker for the treatment's effect on cccDNA, the hepatitis B viral material it is designed to eliminate. Gorsuch also said the first e-antigen-positive patient treated in the study had a 3.7-log reduction in pgRNA to undetectable levels at the 0.4 mg/kg dose selected for the next phase. Despite the encouraging biomarker results, Gorsuch said the remaining question is whether the treatment has eliminated enough cccDNA to produce a viral cure. The Phase II study is intended to answer that question. Story Continues → Alphabet's Most Tempting Valuation Signal May Be Its Most Misleading The study will assess PBGENE-HBV alone and followed by the antisense treatment bepirovirsen. The monotherapy arm will test for viral cure, defined in the discussion as undetectable HBV DNA after treatment is stopped; the combination arm will assess functional cure. Gorsuch said the company sees a potential benefit from reducing viral burden before administering bepirovirsen. Patients in the combination arm will need to meet bepirovirsen eligibility criteria, Gorsuch said. Kelly said Precision had not yet discussed a partnership with GSK but was prepared to purchase bepirovirsen for the study. For patients stopping nucleoside therapy, Gorsuch said normal liver enzymes and fully suppressed HBV DNA are baseline safety considerations. She said regulatory guidance calls for six months off nucleoside treatment to demonstrate an approvable endpoint. Kelly said any withdrawal of therapy in Phase I would be handled case by case, with the larger Phase II study expected to provide more consistent data. Duchenne study awaits biopsy results Precision's Duchenne muscular dystrophy program uses its ARCUS gene-editing technology to remove a region of the dystrophin gene and aims to restore a near full-length dystrophin protein. Gorsuch said the targeted region is mutated in up to 60% of children with the disease. The first patient in the Phase I/II FUNCTION-DMD study had no serious adverse events or adverse events of special interest, Gorsuch said. An independent data safety monitoring board reviewed results through eight weeks after treatment, saw no concerning safety signals and endorsed completing dosing of the first part of the study, she said. Kelly said three-month biopsy data for approximately the first three patients could be available around the second quarter of 2027. The second patient had been enrolled and the third was being screened, he said. Gorsuch said the company believes dystrophin expression above 5% could be therapeutically meaningful, but emphasized that any protein increase must ultimately be linked to functional benefit. Kelly said the first patient's 12-month biopsy data could arrive in the fall of 2027. Gorsuch said the 12-month point would also be more appropriate than three months for beginning to assess functional improvements. About Precision BioSciences (NASDAQ:DTIL) Precision BioSciences is a biotechnology company developing gene-editing therapies using its proprietary ARCUS platform. The platform is designed to make targeted changes to DNA and is being applied to investigational treatments for genetic and infectious diseases. The company's programs include PBGENE-HBV, an investigational therapy designed to target hepatitis B virus DNA, and PBGENE-DMD, a gene-editing program for Duchenne muscular dystrophy. These candidates remain in development and are not approved treatments. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 27, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Hepatitis B Reactivation Risk Differs Across Immunosuppressed Groups, Study Finds by November 26, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Hepatitis B Reactivation Risk Differs Across Immunosuppressed Groups, Study Finds Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A new hybrid evidence synthesis has mapped the risk of hepatitis B virus reactivation across immunocompromised patient groups, revealing substantial variation in reactivation frequency depending on baseline serological status and immunosuppressive exposure. The investigation combined an umbrella review of existing systematic reviews with a de novo meta-analysis of duplicate-free primary studies to clarify reactivation risks that clinicians encounter during immunosuppressive therapy. Hepatitis B virus reactivation represents a preventable yet inconsistently managed complication for individuals undergoing immunosuppressive regimens. While routine antiviral prophylaxis is widely recommended for surface-antigen-positive patients, clinical uncertainty and questions regarding real-world applicability have persisted for patients with resolved infection, those receiving emerging immunotherapies or biologics, solid organ or stem cell transplant recipients, and diverse regional patient populations. To evaluate the existing body of evidence, the research team deployed a structured two-level analytical framework. The first level conducted a review-level synthesis, systematically searching six comprehensive research databases for systematic reviews and meta-analyses published between January 2014 and March 2025. Investigators formally appraised the methodological quality of the retrieved reviews using the AMSTAR-2 tool and calculated the degree of overlap among reviews using the Corrected Covered Area metric. The second level of the framework consisted of a de novo meta-analysis directly aggregating data from primary clinical studies identified across the search results. After removing duplicate entries across overlapping reviews, investigators extracted data from 275 primary studies and applied a random-effects model to compute pooled incidence estimates. Findings across both tiers were subsequently assembled into structured evidence maps categorized by serological markers and specific drug exposures. Across the ten included systematic reviews and meta-analyses, the authors identified critical methodological limitations, noting that the overall methodological quality of the review-level evidence was low or very low. A qualitative narrative synthesis of this literature demonstrated that the observed risk of viral reactivation was highest among individuals positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, followed by individuals displaying a surface-antigen-negative and core-antibody-positive serological profile. The subsequent de novo meta-analysis of the 275 original primary studies provided specific pooled quantitative risk estimates across these distinct serological groups. Among individuals who were surface-antigen positive, the pooled incidence of hepatitis B reactivation was 11.44 percent, with a 95 percent confidence interval spanning from 9.17 percent to 13.86 percent. In contrast, patients with resolved infection defined by negative surface antigen and positive core antibody status demonstrated a pooled reactivation incidence of 0.99 percent, with a 95 percent confidence interval from 0.41 percent to 1.74 percent. Additional subgroup evaluations within the resolved hepatitis B cohort indicated that patients lacking surface antibodies experienced higher reactivation estimates than those with detectable surface antibodies. The data also confirmed that prophylactic antiviral therapy was associated with a lower incidence of viral reactivation among surface-antigen-positive patients undergoing immunosuppressive treatment. The investigators emphasized significant statistical heterogeneity across all conducted subgroup analyses, cautioning that these summary figures reflect an inherently diverse evidence base rather than exact incidence rates directly generalizable to every bedside setting. Furthermore, direct comparative evidence comparing different antiviral agents remains insufficient, as does conclusive evidence demonstrating prophylactic benefit in patients with resolved infection, highlighting the ongoing need for targeted research. supplementary_news.content: Less than two-thirds of newborns got hepatitis B shots in first half of 2026 Watch: Why some parents aren't giving their children the ... Why some parents aren't giving their children the Hep B vaccine WCVB US LIVE Current Time 0:00 / Total Duration 2:27 Sorry, this video is not available, please check back later. Advertisement Updated: 7:08 PM EST Nov 25, 2026 Editorial Standards i Livia Daggett Digital Curator Less than two-thirds of newborns got hepatitis B shots in first half of 2026 Updated: 7:08 PM EST Nov 25, 2026 Editorial Standards i Livia Daggett Digital Curator Less than two-thirds of newborn babies in the U.S. were vaccinated against hepatitis B this year, a drop of nearly 15% from 2020, according to a new study. In a report published this week in the journal NEJM Evidence, researchers found that after reaching an average of 80% from 2020 to 2022, rates of vaccination against hepatitis B for newborns began to decline in 2023, falling to 65.6% in 2026. Advertisement Past video coverage of related study on drop in vaccination rates above. This is the first look at hepatitis B birth vaccination rates after the Centers for Disease Control in December 2025 ended its longstanding recommendation that all babies get the vaccine at birth. Hepatitis B is a virus that can damage the liver and lead to lifelong health problems. The vaccine against it protects against short-term illness and a life-threatening infection called chronic hepatitis B, which is the most common form among newborns. Babies can be exposed to hepatitis B from their mothers, during labor or in the early days of their lives. People often don’t know they are infected with the virus, making it more difficult to prevent transmission. In December 2025, the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, a committee within the CDC that earlier that year had its members replaced with new ones, stopped recommending HBV vaccination for all newborns. It instead recommended parents of babies whose mothers test negative for hepatitis B make a decision with their healthcare providers. The vaccines were still recommended for babies whose mothers tested positive or had an unknown status. CDC panel rolls back hepatitis B vaccine recommendation for newborns “The bottom line is confusion creates inaction among parents,” Dr. Demetre Daskalakis, an author of the study and a former leader at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, told the Wall Street Journal . “It’s as clear as mud what to do because you have public messaging that sheds doubt on the effectiveness of the hepatitis B vaccine.” The change in guidance for hepatitis B vaccination came amid sweeping changes to childhood vaccination recommendations pursued by the Trump administration. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has a history of sowing doubt about vaccines, and after taking office, he dismissed the members of the CDC’s vaccine policy committee and appointed new ones. And in January 2026, the CDC cut its list of vaccines recommended for every child from 17 to 11, one of the biggest changes to childhood disease prevention in decades. However, this study found that hepatitis B vaccination rates for newborns started to drop in 2023, before the CDC’s change, though the decrease continued afterward. The authors said the continuing drop likely reflects “continuing vaccine hesitancy and confusion among parents” after the changes to newborn hepatitis B vaccine recommendations. A separate study on newborn hepatitis B vaccinations from earlier this year pointed to the decline coinciding with a “period of heightened public discourse in the US regarding childhood vaccination following the COVID-19 pandemic.” The American Academy of Pediatrics, the largest professional association of pediatricians in the U.S., continues to recommend that babies receive the shot at birth. American Academy of Pediatrics releases updated children's vaccination recommendations According to a 2024 CDC report , among children born in the U.S. from 1994 to 2023, routine childhood vaccinations will have prevented approximately 508 million lifetime cases of illness, 32 million hospitalizations and 1,129,000 deaths, as well as resulting in direct savings of $540 billion and societal savings of $2.7 trillion. During that same time period, the hepatitis B vaccine that the CDC no longer recommends for all children prevented 6 million cases of hepatitis B and 940,000 hospitalizations, the CDC report said. The report found that hepatitis B birth vaccine doses fell even among babies born to mothers who did test positive for hepatitis B, dropping from an average of around 97% to 98% in 2018-2025 to 93.9% during the first half of 2026. Hepatitis B vaccination at birth drops sharply among US newborns, new NEJM Evidence study finds Truveta Tue, November 24, 2026 at 7:45 AM MST 4 min read Truveta analysis of more than 1.3 million infants finds vaccination rates declining even among newborns at highest risk of infection Hep-B-Research-in-NEJM-Press-Release-Thumbnail-2 Hepatitis B vaccination among US newborns has fallen sharply in recent years, including among infants born to mothers with hepatitis B infection, according to new Truveta research published in NEJM Evidence. HepB-vaccination_NEJM-Evidence_graph-A A new Truveta led study published NEJM Evidence on Nov. 24, 2026, analyzed de-identified electronic health records from more than 1.3 million infants, found that hepatitis B vaccination received within one day of birth declined from approximately 80% in 2022 to 65.6% by June 2026. The decline began in 2023, nearly three years before federal vaccine advisers changed the longstanding recommendation for universal hepatitis B vaccination at birth. Bellevue, Wash., Nov. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Hepatitis B vaccination among US newborns has fallen sharply in recent years, including among infants born to mothers with hepatitis B infection, according to new Truveta research published in NEJM Evidence. The study, which analyzed de-identified electronic health records from more than 1.3 million infants, found that hepatitis B vaccination received within one day of birth declined from approximately 80% in 2022 to 65.6% by June 2026. The decline began in 2023, nearly three years before federal vaccine advisers changed the longstanding recommendation for universal hepatitis B vaccination at birth. Researchers also identified a troubling decline among newborns at greatest risk of infection. From 2020 through 2025, between 97-98% of infants born to mothers who tested positive for hepatitis B received the vaccine at birth. During the first six months of 2026, that rate fell to 93.9%. "The hepatitis B birth dose was designed to protect every newborn, including those whose mothers may not know they're infected," said Nina Masters, PhD, MPH, Principal Research Scientist at Truveta and the paper's lead author. "No screening system is perfect. That's why it's so concerning to see vaccination declining across the board, even among babies whose mothers have tested positive for hepatitis B." Hepatitis B can be transmitted from mother to child during birth, making timely vaccination especially important. Yet despite widespread prenatal screening, researchers found that approximately one in 10 pregnancies had no recorded hepatitis B test. Applied to roughly 3.6 million births in the US each year, that screening gap could affect an estimated 360,000 newborns annually. Based on the infection rate observed in the study, researchers estimate that more than 640 infants each year could be born to mothers whose hepatitis B infection went undetected during pregnancy. Masters added that these findings underscore the importance of the hepatitis B birth-dose vaccination as a safeguard against infections that might otherwise be missed. The study lands amid significant changes to US vaccine policy. In December 2025, federal vaccine advisers voted to end the longstanding recommendation for universal hepatitis B vaccination at birth, followed by broader changes to the childhood immunization schedule in January. A federal judge temporarily blocked those decisions in March 2026, restoring the previous recommendations while litigation continued. Story Continues While the decline in birth-dose vaccination began well before these policy decisions, the findings raise new concerns about gaps in protection that were already emerging. "We're talking about a vaccine that has protected generations of children from a potentially devastating infection. And now we're seeing fewer newborns receive it—even those we know are at greatest risk," said Demetre C. Daskalakis, MD, MPH, a study co-author and the former director of the CDC's National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases. "These numbers aren't just a trend line. Each data point represents a real child who may be left vulnerable to a preventable disease. At a time when vaccine policy is changing, we need more evidence guiding our decisions, not less." The study, "Hepatitis B Birth Dose Vaccination in the United States: January 2018 – June 2026," analyzed de-identified electronic health records from 1,338,961 infants born to more than one million mothers. Researchers used linked maternal and infant records to examine prenatal hepatitis B screening and vaccination following birth. The study was authored by Nina B. Masters, PhD, MPH; Brianna M. G. Cartwright, MS; Karen Gilbert Farrar, PhD; Johnathan M. Lancaster, MD, PhD; and Demetre C. Daskalakis, MD, MPH. About Truveta Truveta transforms healthcare into intelligence. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 27, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Hepatitis B Virus Genomic Integration Patterns Reveal Preferential Sites Associated With Hepatocarcinogenesis by November 23, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Hepatitis B Virus Genomic Integration Patterns Reveal Preferential Sites Associated With Hepatocarcinogenesis Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Hepatitis B virus genomic integrations into the human genome occur across nearly all chromosomes but show marked enrichment in specific chromosomal ends, proximal promoters, CpG islands, and cancer-associated genes, according to a comprehensive in silico genomic analysis published in In Silico Research in Biomedicine. Researchers Deyou Tang, Wensheng Yang, and Juan Fu conducted a large-scale computational evaluation of 29,153 distinct Hepatitis B virus integration sites to resolve long-standing discrepancies regarding where viral DNA inserts and how these insertions relate to the development of hepatocellular carcinoma. By establishing a normalized analytical framework, the authors identified distinct genomic preferences that separate viral insertion events occurring in liver tumor tissues from those found in non-tumor counterparts, clarifying structural and functional mechanisms underlying viral hepatocarcinogenesis. Hepatocellular carcinoma represents a primary liver malignancy with Hepatitis B virus infection serving as a predominant pathogenic driver worldwide. Chronic infection permits viral DNA to integrate directly into the host hepatocyte genome, an event recognized to promote oncogenic transformation through multiple cellular disruptions including chromosomal instability, insertional mutagenesis in key cancer genes, and cis-activation of neighboring transcripts. Despite decades of study, earlier characterizations of recurrent integration hotspots showed persistent inconsistencies beyond a few recognized genes such as telomerase reverse transcriptase and Cyclin E1. Previous investigations had also diverged regarding whether insertions favored specific functional chromatin regions or fragile sites, variations largely attributable to limited cohort sizes, tumor heterogeneity, different viral sub-genotypes, and diverse detection methodologies across independent laboratories. Discover more Cancer Order DNA Kits Find Study Aids To overcome these methodological variations and sample-size limitations, the researchers constructed a curated reference resource by assembling 36,009 raw viral integration sites from 21 published articles and the Viral Integration Sites Database. The team applied rigorous curation criteria, discarding records lacking chromosomal coordinates or valid chromosome numbers, eliminating unlocalized scaffolds and mitochondrial hits, and restricting candidate assemblies to GRCh37 and GRCh38 before systematically converting all valid loci to reference genome GRCh38.p14 via the NCBI Genome Remapping Service. Integrations located within twelve nucleotides of each other were merged into unified central coordinates, and duplicated entries from overlapping reports were eliminated. The final curated catalog comprised 29,153 unique viral integration sites, containing 12,759 sites identified in liver tumor tissues, 15,834 in adjacent non-tumor tissues, 1,151 in cell-free circulating DNA, and 290 in cell line models. Discover more Check Symptoms Study Biology cancer Find Cancer Care Assessing insertion density across varying chromosomal lengths required a standardized comparative metric capable of controlling for cohort-level and regional variability. The investigators developed an analytical measurement defined as the number of Hepatitis B virus integration sites per million nucleotides, abbreviated as VPM. This formula factored the site count in a given target region, the base-pair length of that region, the total integration tally across the dataset, and the specific integration tally within the corresponding tissue class. Furthermore, the baseline expected density over autosomes and sex chromosomes was adjusted by incorporating the demographic sex ratio derived from the clinical records, resulting in an expected baseline of 9.74 integrations per million nucleotides for autosomes, 5.89 for chromosome X, and 3.85 for chromosome Y. Hypothesized integration frequencies were modeled through binomial distributions and evaluated against expected distributions via Z-tests and chi-square tests. At the gross chromosomal level, viral insertion events were identified spanning nearly the entire human genome, targeting 831 of the 862 cytobands recognized in standard genomic annotations, equivalent to 96.4 percent of all cytobands. However, statistically significant insertion densities clustered in specific structural zones, with tumors exhibiting significantly elevated insertion rates compared to non-tumor tissues on chromosomes 5, 8, 17, 19, and Y. Notably, chromosome Y demonstrated an integration density in tumor specimens that was twice as high as that observed in non-tumor tissues, an observation that aligns with the established clinical epidemiological disparity showing higher hepatocellular carcinoma incidence in males than females. While centromeric regions showed an absence of viral enrichment, terminal chromosomal zones displayed strong insertional biases, with the average density in cytobands nearest to telomeres reaching roughly double the genome-wide expectation. Discover more Genomic genomics genomic Fine-scale mapping of chromosomal extremities revealed that peak viral insertion density did not reside directly at the physical telomeric ends, but concentrated preferentially within a window 100 kilobase pairs from the chromosome extremities, where tumor tissues overwhelmed non-tumor tissue rates. Within this terminal 100-kilobase-pair perimeter, integration sites exhibited asymmetric preferences, clustering unevenly toward either the short p-arm or long q-arm of individual chromosomes. The authors noted that recurring integration in telomeric vicinities involves microhomology-mediated repair processes with guanine-rich repetitive telomeric sequences, a phenomenon known to induce complex structural rearrangements, telomerase binding irregularities, extensive DNA amplification, and terminal deletions during early hepatocarcinogenesis. When examining functional genomic architecture, the team determined that Hepatitis B virus insertions were significantly enriched within CpG islands, proximal promoter regions located within one kilobase pair of transcription start sites, and 3-prime untranslated regions. Conversely, integration occurred without significant preference in chromosomal fragile regions or open chromatin regions relative to baseline statistical expectations. Proximity evaluations around CpG islands demonstrated that integration frequency was highest directly within the islands and steadily declined as distance increased outward through two and ten kilobase pairs. Tumor tissues exhibited significantly elevated insertion density in CpG islands relative to non-tumor tissues, as well as in the CpG island shores of chromosomes 4, 5, 17, 18, 19, and 21. Because CpG islands and promoters frequently harbor GC-rich short direct repeats that align with viral DNA ends during host repair, structural integration can disrupt methylation dynamics and perturb normal transcriptional control. Analysis of gene structural domains revealed that 17.96 percent of all integrations mapped to promoters, 33 percent fell within introns, and 45.91 percent localized to distal intergenic regions. In tumor tissues, proximal promoter insertions within one kilobase pair were significantly elevated compared to non-tumor counterparts. Furthermore, viral insertions concentrated disproportionately in cancer-associated genes, particularly oncogenes over tumor suppressor genes. Cancer genes accounted for 15.1 percent of integration sites restricted to tumor samples compared to only 4.6 percent of sites found exclusively in non-tumor tissues, while genes demonstrating integration across both tissue types showed an 18.6 percent cancer-association rate. Highly recurrent insertion targets included recognized drivers such as telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), lysine methyltransferase 2B (KMT2B), Cyclin E1 (CCNE1), Cyclin A2 (CCNA2), and Albumin (ALB), with insertions frequently occupying the promoter domains of TERT, CCNA2, and CCNE1 and the 3-prime untranslated region of KMT2B. To connect physical integration hotspots with transcriptional consequences, the researchers evaluated gene expression data from 371 hepatocellular carcinoma samples in The Cancer Genome Atlas, stratified into four distinct cohorts: HBV-infected tumors, HBV-uninfected tumors, HBV-infected non-tumor tissues, and HBV-uninfected non-tumor tissues. Pairwise differential expression analysis demonstrated substantial transcriptional remodeling in tumor tissues compared to rare expression changes in non-tumor cohorts. Candidate integration genes and their immediate upstream and downstream flanking genes exhibited pronounced transcriptional divergence. Specifically, the expression changes for TERT, CCNE1, and Alpha fetoprotein (AFP) were markedly amplified in HBV-infected comparisons relative to uninfected groups. Elevated AFP transcription in infected tumors was highlighted as an external regulatory effect linked to adjacent viral insertions within the neighboring Albumin locus, illustrating insertional cis-effects on neighboring gene expression. Pathway enrichment of differentially expressed genes with multiple integration events revealed pronounced alterations in critical cellular processes, including transmembrane transport, cAMP signaling, calcium signaling, and the cytochrome P450 pathway. The investigators observed significant differences in monocarboxylic acid metabolic processes and oxoacid metabolism specifically within HBV-infected comparative groups that were absent in uninfected comparisons. Functional interactions between dysregulated genes highlight converging mechanisms of hepatocarcinogenesis, wherein TERT-mediated telomere lengthening and CCNE1-driven G1/S transition promote uncontrolled cell cycle progression, while KMT2B modifications alter histone methylation and DNA repair checkpoints. Metabolic adjustments facilitated by AFP and carbamoyl-phosphate synthase 1 (CPS1) further sustain proliferative demands, establishing a multifaceted oncogenic network. The authors underscored several study limitations inherent to their data integration strategy. Because the curated dataset aggregated genomic coordinates from published literature and databases without uniform access to raw sequence reads, breakpoint-level motif signatures and microhomology sequences could not be independently reconstructed. Furthermore, technical variations across diverse sequencing platforms, library depths, patient age distributions, tumor stages, and viral subtypes could introduce detection biases. The authors also emphasized that because the Cancer Genome Atlas lacks concurrent viral integration sequencing for the same specimens, direct causal connections between specific insertional breakpoints and individual transcriptomic alterations remain preliminary, requiring targeted experimental and multi-center validation in prospective clinical cohorts. MMP9 expression distinguished all five occult hepatitis B samples from five healthy controls. Findings supported further investigation of MMP9 for early liver injury risk assessment. OCCULT hepatitis B virus infection may be associated with a distinctive blood gene expression signature, with MMP9 emerging as a potential biomarker for identifying patients at risk of liver injury, according to an exploratory transcriptomic analysis. The findings followed a clinical case involving rapid progression from genotype C occult hepatitis B infection to advanced hepatocellular carcinoma, highlighting the need for improved risk stratification. Occult Hepatitis B Presents Diagnostic Challenges Occult hepatitis B virus infection is characterised by undetectable hepatitis B surface antigen despite detectable viral DNA, creating challenges for identifying and monitoring affected patients. Currently, validated biomarkers for predicting liver injury or disease progression in this population remain unavailable. Researchers reported a patient with genotype C occult hepatitis B infection who rapidly developed advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. This case prompted an exploratory investigation into potential molecular markers associated with occult infection. The researchers reanalysed a publicly available transcriptomic dataset containing peripheral blood mononuclear cell samples from individuals with occult hepatitis B and healthy controls. Differential gene expression analysis was performed to identify candidate biomarkers, followed by sensitivity testing to assess the consistency of the findings. MMP9 Expression Distinguishes Occult Hepatitis B Samples The analysis identified 1,930 differentially expressed genes between the occult hepatitis B and control groups. Among these, MMP9, which encodes matrix metalloproteinase 9, demonstrated one of the strongest transcriptional signals (log2 fold change: 10.69; adjusted p=6.13×10−36). All five occult hepatitis B samples expressed MMP9 at substantially higher levels than the five healthy controls. Raw expression counts ranged from 547–25,598 in the infection group, compared with 2–8 among controls, with no overlap between groups. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated complete separation (area under the curve: 1.000), with sensitivity and specificity both reaching 100% (95% CI: 56–100% for each). However, these estimates were derived from only 10 samples and require cautious interpretation. Biomarker Findings Require Prospective Validation Sensitivity analyses further supported the consistency of the MMP9 transcriptional signal. Across 10 leave-one-out iterations, MMP9 remained among the highest-ranked genes, with consistently increased expression (log2 fold change: 10.52–10.81). The mean number of differentially expressed genes across these analyses was 1,901, with a coefficient of variation of 5%. Researchers suggested that MMP9 could represent an early-warning candidate biomarker for occult hepatitis B-related liver injury. Nevertheless, the study did not establish that MMP9 predicts future hepatocellular carcinoma, and the small discovery cohort limits generalisability. The findings also require validation in independent populations before clinical risk assessment applications can be considered. Overall, the analysis identified a promising molecular signal that warrants prospective investigation to determine its relationship with liver injury and disease progression in occult hepatitis B infection. Reference Liu X et al. Occult Hepatitis B Virus Genotype C Infection with Rapid Progression to Advanced Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Clinical Case and Exploratory Transcriptomic Analysis Identifying MMP9 as an Early-Warning Candidate Biomarker,” be used for publication. The findings followed a clinical case involving rapid progression from genotype C occult hepatitis B infection to advanced hepatocellular carcinoma, highlighting the need for improved risk stratification. Occult Hepatitis B Presents Diagnostic Challenges. Occult hepatitis B virus infection is characterised by undetectable hepatitis B surface antigen despite detectable viral DNA, creating challenges for identifying and monitoring affected patients. Currently, validated biomarkers for predicting liver injury or disease progression in this population remain unavailable. Researchers reported a patient with genotype C occult hepatitis B infection who rapidly developed advanced hepatocellular carcinoma. This case prompted an exploratory investigation into potential molecular markers associated with occult infection. The researchers reanalysed a publicly available transcriptomic dataset containing peripheral blood mononuclear cell samples from individuals with occult hepatitis B and healthy controls. Differential gene expression analysis was performed to identify candidate biomarkers, followed by sensitivity testing to assess the consistency of the findings. MMP9 Expression Distinguishes Occult Hepatitis B Samples. The analysis identified 1,930 differentially expressed genes between the occult hepatitis B and control groups. Among these, MMP9, which encodes matrix metalloproteinase 9, demonstrated one of the strongest transcriptional signals (log2 fold change: 10.69; adjusted p=6.13×10−36). All five occult hepatitis B samples expressed MMP9 at substantially higher levels than the five healthy controls. Raw expression counts ranged from 547–25,598 in the infection group, compared with 2–8 among controls, with no overlap between groups. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated complete separation (area under the curve: 1.000), with sensitivity and specificity both reaching 100% (95% CI: 56–100% for each). However, these estimates were derived from only 10 samples and require cautious interpretation. Biomarker Findings Require Prospective Validation. Sensitivity analyses further supported the consistency of the MMP9 transcriptional signal. Across 10 leave-one-out iterations, MMP9 remained among the highest-ranked genes, with consistently increased expression (log2 fold change: 10.52–10.81). The mean number of differentially expressed genes across these analyses was 1,901, with a coefficient of variation of 5%. Researchers suggested that MMP9 could represent an early-warning candidate biomarker for occult hepatitis B-related liver injury. Nevertheless, the study did not establish that MMP9 predicts future hepatocellular carcinoma, and the small discovery cohort limits generalisability. The findings also require validation in independent populations before clinical risk assessment applications can be considered. Overall, the analysis identified a promising molecular signal that warrants prospective investigation to determine its relationship with liver injury and disease progression in occult hepatitis B infection. supplementary_news.content_title: The number of babies getting vaccinated for hepatitis B at birth is dropping precipitously
supplementary_news.content: The number of babies getting vaccinated for hepatitis B at birth is dropping precipitously Hepatitis B, which can be passed from mother to baby, is a liver disease that can be fatal if left untreated Join Our Community of Science Lovers! The number of babies born in U.S. who received a vaccine for hepatitis B within a day of birth has dropped sharply, according to a new study. Researchers at the health data firm Truveta and Callen-Lorde Community Health Center in New York City examined anonymized electronic health records from more than 1.3 million infants and found the percentage who received the shot within 24 hours of being born had fallen from 80 percent in 2022 to just 65.6 percent in 2026. The decline extended to babies who were most at risk: up to 98 percent of mothers who tested positive for hepatitis B got their babies vaccinated in 2022, but that had fallen to just under 94 percent in 2026, the study found. The findings were published in the journal NEJM Evidence on Tuesday. If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing . By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today. “The hepatitis B birth dose was designed to protect every newborn, including those whose mothers may not know they’re infected,” said Nina Masters, principal research scientist at Truveta and the study’s lead author, in a statement. “No screening system is perfect. That’s why it’s so concerning to see vaccination declining across the board, even among babies whose mothers have tested positive for hepatitis B.” Hepatitis B is a liver disease that can, if left untreated, lead to liver cancer or even death. The disease is transmissible through body fluids and can be passed from mother to baby in the womb. By extrapolating their data to the 3.6 million births that occur in the U.S. each year, the researchers concluded that as many as 360,000 infants are likely going without the shot. While prenatal screening is widely available, they also estimated that roughly 640 unvaccinated babies may be born to mothers who have been infected with hepatitis B but have not been screened. The number of unvaccinated infants is “alarming,” says Michael Osterholm, director of the Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy. “They represent children who will develop chronic hepatitis B infections, cirrhosis of the liver and liver cancer,” he says. “They also send a clear signal to federal health leaders that they need a plan to address increasing rates of vaccine hesitancy other than misleadingly blaming it on the pandemic.” In December 2025 the CDC’s vaccine advisory panel eliminated a decades-old recommendation that the hepatitis B vaccine be given universally at birth. Instead the panel recommended parents consult with a health care provider about when to give their baby the child’s first dose of the vaccine as long as the mother has tested negative for the disease. The change quickly drew fire from public health experts, who said the decision ran contrary to the evidence and would increase infants’ vulnerability to infection. The new study shows that vaccination rates were already declining before that policy change. The number of unvaccinated babies identified in the study grew from 20,473 in 2018 to more than 34,000 in 2022, peaking at more than 64,500 in 2025. “We’re talking about a vaccine that has protected generations of children from a potentially devastating infection,” said study co-author Demetre Daskalakis, chief medical officer at Callen-Lorde and former director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Illness, in the same statement. “And now we’re seeing fewer newborns receive it—even those we know are at greatest risk. These numbers aren’t just a trend line. Each data point represents a real child who may be left vulnerable to a preventable disease. At a time when vaccine policy is changing, we need more evidence guiding our decisions, not less.” Great science journalism requires human expertise, time, effort and creativity. And it costs money. supplementary_news.content_title: Precision BioSciences Targets Hepatitis B Cure in Phase II, Eyes Duchenne Data in 2027
supplementary_news.content: Precision BioSciences Targets Hepatitis B Cure in Phase II, Eyes Duchenne Data in 2027 3 min read DTIL −0.49% Precision BioSciences DTIL plans to advance its hepatitis B gene-editing treatment into a Phase II study and expects initial biopsy results from its Duchenne muscular dystrophy program in 2027, executives said at a Jefferies conference. Chief Scientific Officer Cassie Gorsuch said the hepatitis B study will test whether the company’s treatment, PBGENE-HBV, can reduce enough of the viral material known as cccDNA to achieve a viral cure. Chief Operating Officer Alex Kelly said the company expects to begin seeing Phase II data in the second half of 2027. Kelly also said Precision had $108 million in cash as of Sept. 30 and recently raised $125 million, taking its cash balance above $200 million. He said the company’s cash runway extends into the fourth quarter of 2029. Hepatitis B program moves toward Phase II Gorsuch said 25 patients had received PBGENE-HBV in the repeat-dose Phase I study, with 59 administrations across the group. At a recent liver meeting, the company reported that six patients with at least six months of follow-up after their pregenomic RNA, or pgRNA, became undetectable continued to have undetectable levels. The company views pgRNA as a primary biomarker for the treatment’s effect on cccDNA, the hepatitis B viral material it is designed to eliminate. Gorsuch also said the first e-antigen-positive patient treated in the study had a 3.7-log reduction in pgRNA to undetectable levels at the 0.4 mg/kg dose selected for the next phase. Despite the encouraging biomarker results, Gorsuch said the remaining question is whether the treatment has eliminated enough cccDNA to produce a viral cure. The Phase II study is intended to answer that question. The study will assess PBGENE-HBV alone and followed by the antisense treatment bepirovirsen. The monotherapy arm will test for viral cure, defined in the discussion as undetectable HBV DNA after treatment is stopped; the combination arm will assess functional cure. Gorsuch said the company sees a potential benefit from reducing viral burden before administering bepirovirsen. Patients in the combination arm will need to meet bepirovirsen eligibility criteria, Gorsuch said. Kelly said Precision had not yet discussed a partnership with GSK but was prepared to purchase bepirovirsen for the study. For patients stopping nucleoside therapy, Gorsuch said normal liver enzymes and fully suppressed HBV DNA are baseline safety considerations. She said regulatory guidance calls for six months off nucleoside treatment to demonstrate an approvable endpoint. Kelly said any withdrawal of therapy in Phase I would be handled case by case, with the larger Phase II study expected to provide more consistent data. Duchenne study awaits biopsy results Precision’s Duchenne muscular dystrophy program uses its ARCUS gene-editing technology to remove a region of the dystrophin gene and aims to restore a near full-length dystrophin protein. Gorsuch said the targeted region is mutated in up to 60% of children with the disease. The first patient in the Phase I/II FUNCTION-DMD study had no serious adverse events or adverse events of special interest, Gorsuch said. An independent data safety monitoring board reviewed results through eight weeks after treatment, saw no concerning safety signals and endorsed completing dosing of the first part of the study, she said. Kelly said three-month biopsy data for approximately the first three patients could be available around the second quarter of 2027. The second patient had been enrolled and the third was being screened, he said. Gorsuch said the company believes dystrophin expression above 5% could be therapeutically meaningful, but emphasized that any protein increase must ultimately be linked to functional benefit. Kelly said the first patient’s 12-month biopsy data could arrive in the fall of 2027. Gorsuch said the 12-month point would also be more appropriate than three months for beginning to assess functional improvements. About Precision BioSciences DTIL Precision BioSciences is a biotechnology company developing gene-editing therapies using its proprietary ARCUS platform. The platform is designed to make targeted changes to DNA and is being applied to investigational treatments for genetic and infectious diseases. The company's programs include PBGENE-HBV, an investigational therapy designed to target hepatitis B virus DNA, and PBGENE-DMD, a gene-editing program for Duchenne muscular dystrophy. These candidates remain in development and are not approved treatments. Tags: Hepatitis B HIV Glasgow 2026 Long-Acting Antiretrovirals Share: aidsmap news story Although hepatitis B reactivation is rare after a switch to injectable cabotegravir/rilpivirine, people with HIV require careful monitoring before and after a switch to assess protection against hepatitis B and reactivation risks, studies presented at HIV Glasgow 2026 suggest. Cohort studies carried out in Spain and Italy found that rates of hepatitis B reactivation after switching to injectable cabotegravir/rilpivirine were low or non-existent. But the Italian study highlighted the risk of poor or non-existent immunity to hepatitis B despite vaccination. Three vaccinated people acquired hepatitis B during the study, although their infections were asymptomatic and detected only through tests for hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) and surface antibody (anti-HBs). supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 27, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health MRN-ATM Pathway Activates During CD4+ T-Cell Senescence in Chronic Hepatitis B by November 21, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 MRN-ATM Pathway Activates During CD4+ T-Cell Senescence in Chronic Hepatitis B Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram People with chronic hepatitis B exhibit a senescence-associated phenotype in their CD4+ T cells compared to healthy individuals, according to research published in Clinical and Experimental Medicine. The study demonstrated that CD4+ T cells from patients with chronic hepatitis B displayed elevated levels of KLRG1, accompanied by increased genomic DNA damage and telomere shortening. Alongside these cellular alterations, investigators identified prominent activation of the MRE11/RAD50/NBS1-ataxia telangiectasia mutated (MRN-ATM) pathway in CD4+ T cells from individuals with chronic hepatitis B virus infection. In persistent viral infections, T-cell senescence represents a hallmark of immune dysfunction characterized by the accumulation of DNA damage and telomere attrition, though the precise role of the DNA damage response pathway in CD4+ T cells during chronic infection has remained poorly defined. Targeted experimental interventions demonstrated that suppressing MRN attenuated ATM phosphorylation and its downstream signaling molecules. Furthermore, inhibition of ATM reduced the production of interferon-gamma and interleukin-2 in CD4+ T lymphocytes isolated from both individuals with chronic hepatitis B and healthy subjects. Discover more Find Senior Care Study Biology Check Symptoms Study Anatomy Get Tested The findings indicate that concurrent activation of the MRN-ATM pathway during chronic hepatitis B virus infection may represent a mechanism that repairs genomic DNA damage and associates with CD4+ T-cell cytokine production, although it does not fully prevent senescence. The authors noted that elucidating the relationship between this senescence-associated phenotype and the MRN-ATM pathway provides insight into the mechanisms underlying viral persistence and may inform future therapeutic strategies. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 27, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health MRN-ATM Pathway Activates During CD4+ T-Cell Senescence in Chronic Hepatitis B by November 21, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 MRN-ATM Pathway Activates During CD4+ T-Cell Senescence in Chronic Hepatitis B Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram People with chronic hepatitis B exhibit a senescence-associated phenotype in their CD4+ T cells compared to healthy individuals, according to research published in Clinical and Experimental Medicine. The study demonstrated that CD4+ T cells from patients with chronic hepatitis B displayed elevated levels of KLRG1, accompanied by increased genomic DNA damage and telomere shortening. Alongside these cellular alterations, investigators identified prominent activation of the MRE11/RAD50/NBS1-ataxia telangiectasia mutated (MRN-ATM) pathway in CD4+ T cells from individuals with chronic hepatitis B virus infection. In persistent viral infections, T-cell senescence represents a hallmark of immune dysfunction characterized by the accumulation of DNA damage and telomere attrition, though the precise role of the DNA damage response pathway in CD4+ T cells during chronic infection has remained poorly defined. Targeted experimental interventions demonstrated that suppressing MRN attenuated ATM phosphorylation and its downstream signaling molecules. Furthermore, inhibition of ATM reduced the production of interferon-gamma and interleukin-2 in CD4+ T lymphocytes isolated from both individuals with chronic hepatitis B and healthy subjects. The findings indicate that concurrent activation of the MRN-ATM pathway during chronic hepatitis B virus infection may represent a mechanism that repairs genomic DNA damage and associates with CD4+ T-cell cytokine production, although it does not fully prevent senescence. The authors noted that elucidating the relationship between this senescence-associated phenotype and the MRN-ATM pathway provides insight into the mechanisms underlying viral persistence and may inform future therapeutic strategies. “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Open access 慢性乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染仍是重大全球健康负担。核苷(酸)类似物(NAs)可抑制病毒复制并降低疾病进展,但乙肝表面抗原(HBsAg)清除仍较少见。因此,治疗目标日益聚焦于功能治愈,而持续性HBsAg清除是其核心终点。聚乙二醇干扰素α(PEG-IFNα)为有限疗程治疗方案,可在特定患者中诱导HBsAg清除。定量HBsAg是研究最为充分的治疗中标志物,第12周和第24周检测可为反应指导治疗提供依据;其他病毒标志物如HBV RNA和乙型肝炎核心相关抗原(HBcrAg)亦受关注,但其相关性随乙型肝炎e抗原(HBeAg)状态、治疗策略和人群而异。常规血液学和肝脏生化指标的连续监测证据仍较有限,且既往研究中生物标志物评估与结局判定时窗高度重叠,限制了时间先后顺序的判断。因此,早期实验室变化是否先于后续HBsAg清除,以及哪一时间区间最具信息价值,仍不明确。 研究人员在一项接受聚乙二醇干扰素α-2b(PEG-IFNα-2b)治疗的回顾性双中心队列中解决了这一问题,采用第24周里程碑设计,将早期血液学和肝脏生化变化与后续HBsAg清除相分离。 主要发现包括:第12至24周期间淋巴细胞恢复幅度更大,与后续HBsAg清除相关;该关联在校正治疗中HBsAg动力学后依然存在;纳入淋巴细胞变化后, optimism校正后的曲线下面积(AUC)由0.757升至0.805;潜在轨迹类别与HBsAg清除无显著关联。 慢性乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染仍是全球重大疾病负担,现有核苷(酸)类似物(NAs)虽能有效抑制病毒复制,却极少实现乙肝表面抗原(HBsAg)清除。随着治疗目标向功能治愈转变,持续性HBsAg清除已成为核心终点。聚乙二醇干扰素α(PEG-IFNα)作为有限疗程方案,可在部分患者中诱导HBsAg清除,但疗效存在显著个体差异。目前,定量HBsAg的第12周和第24周动力学是主流的反应指导标志物,HBV RNA与乙型肝炎核心相关抗原(HBcrAg)等新型标志物亦受关注。然而,关于常规血液学与肝脏生化指标动态变化的研究证据有限,且既往分析中标志物测量与结局判定在时间上高度重叠,难以确立早期实验室变化与后续HBsAg清除的先后关系。基于此,研究人员利用第24周里程碑设计,在双中心队列中系统评估了早期常规实验室指标动态对后续HBsAg清除的预测价值。 欢迎索取义翘神州凋亡检测试剂盒最新资料领 取 本研究为回顾性双中心里程碑队列研究,队列来源于天津市第一中心医院(2023—2026年)与天津市第三中心医院(2019—2026年)接受PEG-IFNα-2b治疗的成人慢性HBV感染者,共纳入269例符合里程碑条件的患者。主要技术方法包括:第24周里程碑设计与离散时间生存分析(complementary log-log模型)以分离暴露窗口与结局窗口;线性混合效应模型刻画8项常规指标(白细胞、中性粒细胞、淋巴细胞、单核细胞、血小板、丙氨酸转氨酶(ALT)、天冬氨酸转氨酶(AST)、直接胆红素(DBIL))的早期轨迹;潜在类别混合模型(latent class mixed model)识别轨迹亚型;并通过Bootstrap内部验证、校正多重比较及增量预测指标(AUC、C-index、Brier评分、连续净重分类改善(NRI)、综合判别改善(IDI))评估模型性能。 研究得出的核心结论是:第12至24周期间淋巴细胞计数的回升幅度,是后续第24至72周内HBsAg清除的独立正相关因素;该关联在校正年龄、性别、第24周log?? HBsAg及第12周淋巴细胞计数后依然稳健,且不受基线HBsAg水平、年龄、性别、HBeAg状态及治疗方案影响。将这一动态指标加入临床模型后, optimism校正的72周AUC由0.757提升至0.805,提示其具备增量预测价值。 关键技术方法概括(不超过250字):研究基于天津两家三级医院2019—2026年真实世界队列,采用第24周里程碑框架切分暴露与结局;以线性混合效应模型比较清除组与非清除组在基线、第12周、第24周的8项常规指标轨迹差异;用离散时间互补log-log生存模型评估各时间窗变化量(每1个标准差)与后续清除的风险比(HR);辅以潜在类别混合模型提炼轨迹亚型,并以1000次Bootstrap做 optimism校正,计算AUC、C-index、Brier评分、NRI与IDI完成增量预测验证;多重比较采用Benjamini–Hochberg与Holm校正。 3.1 患者特征 里程碑队列共269例,47例(17.5%)在第24周后至第72周内实现HBsAg清除。清除组更年轻(P<0.001)、体质指数(BMI)更低(P=0.001)、基线HBsAg更低(P<0.001)、γ-谷氨酰转移酶(GGT)更低(P=0.008);初始方案中富马酸丙酚替诺福韦(TAF)联合PEG-IFNα-2b占比更高(P=0.030)。其余血液学与生化基线指标组间无显著差异。 3.2 早期血液学与生化指标的纵向变化 线性混合模型显示,两组淋巴细胞均在第0至12周下降,随后第12至24周清除组回升、非清除组维持低位;组间变化差为0.325×10?/L(95% CI 0.141–0.509,Holm校正P=0.002),整体交互P=0.002(FDR校正P=0.019)。单核细胞第12至24周变化呈名义差异(Holm P=0.016),ALT交互P=0.035,但经FDR校正后均不再显著;白细胞、血小板、中性粒细胞、AST、DBIL无显著轨迹差异。 3.3 早期实验室变化与后续HBsAg清除的关联 离散时间生存模型(模型C,校正第12周起始值、年龄、性别、第24周log?? HBsAg)显示:基线至第12周无任何指标经FDR校正后显著;基线至第24周淋巴细胞变化HR=1.83(95% CI 1.19–2.83,P=0.006)但FDR P=0.074未达显著;第12至24周淋巴细胞每升高1个标准差,清除风险HR=1.93(95% CI 1.43–2.62,P<0.001,FDR P<0.001),为唯一显著项。时间异质性检验无显著差异(P=0.504)。 3.4 增量预测价值与内部验证 在267例完整数据中,加入第12至24周淋巴细胞变化后:相比仅含第24周HBsAg模型,optimism校正ΔAUC=0.060;相比临床模型(年龄、性别、第12周淋巴细胞、第24周HBsAg),AUC由0.757升至0.805(ΔAUC=0.048),C-index由0.802升至0.829,Brier由0.170降至0.159,连续NRI=0.497,IDI=0.046;校准斜率约0.54,提示预测风险偏极端。 3.5 潜在轨迹模式 潜在类别混合模型仅中性粒细胞与AST保留两类别解;白细胞、淋巴细胞、单核细胞、ALT、DBIL因类别比例<10%或分类质量不足归为单类。中性粒细胞两型均为先降后部分回升(低水平型n=238,高水平型n=31);AST两型分别为一过性升高后下降(n=241)与持续明显升高(n=28)。 3.6 轨迹类别与后续清除 校正后高水平中性粒细胞型vs低水平型HR=0.89(95% CI 0.38–2.09,P=0.781);持续AST升高型vs一过性型HR=2.01(95% CI 0.81–4.95,P=0.130)。两者均无统计学显著关联。 3.7 亚组分析 第12至24周淋巴细胞回升的HR在各亚组点估计均>1:基线HBsAg≤1500 IU/mL者HR=1.98(P<0.001),女性HR=2.18(P=0.006),HBeAg阴性HR=1.92(P<0.001),TAF+IFN组HR=3.72(P<0.001),TDF+IFN组HR=2.11(P<0.001);交互检验均不显著(P>0.05),HBeAg阳性仅1例事件无法估计。 3.8 敏感性分析 排除第24周前已清除者后中性粒细胞轨迹结论不变;岭回归校正HBsAg第12至24周降幅、HBeAg、方案后HR=1.60(95% CI 1.15–2.03);限制HBV DNA低于检测下限者HR=1.90(P<0.001);Benjamini–Yekutieli校正后P=0.002仍显著。 讨论部分总结:该双中心里程碑队列将常规实验室窗口与结局窗口在时间上分离,证实“第12至24周淋巴细胞回升”而非“基线到第12周下降”才是与后续HBsAg清除相关的信号,且在校正治疗中HBsAg后仍独立存在。总淋巴细胞计数无法区分效应/调节亚群、细胞再分布或功能活化,既往单细胞研究提示初始/记忆T细胞比例与CD8? T细胞细胞毒性变化可能参与其中,但本研究未做免疫表型,故不推断机制。局限包括回顾性便利样本、两中心入组年代不同未校正中心与时间、剂量/中断/疗程记录不全、肝硬化与基线HBV DNA残余混杂、三次采样无法捕捉瞬时最低点、事件数偏少致亚组精度不足、结局为“首次记录清除”而非持续功能治愈。意义在于:淋巴细胞第12至24周回升是常规、廉价、可重复获取的响应标志物候选,值得前瞻性标准化采样与免疫表型验证后再用于反应指导策略。 结论翻译:在校正治疗中HBsAg后,第12至24周期间的淋巴细胞恢复与后续HBsAg清除相关。其作为常规可用反应标志物的价值,有待前瞻性验证。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! 从2000到2026,27载全因有您;您的每一分支持,都给予我们无穷的动力! 公测期:打赏8元解锁30天免费阅读! 下载安捷伦电子书《通过细胞代谢揭示新的药物靶点》探索如何通过代谢分析促进您的药物发现研究 10x Genomics新品Visium HD 开启单细胞分辨率的全转录组空间分析! 欢迎下载Twist《不断变化的CRISPR筛选格局》电子书 下载《细胞内蛋白质互作分析方法电子书》 引领行业 | 聚焦麦特绘谱代谢组学整体解决方案>> 「大小鼠繁育与健康管理」指导海报,点击即可免费领取电子版或实体海报>> 揭秘单细胞测序-深入了解这项正在改变我们开展科学研究的技术>> 18,000+ 成品模型现货随取,点击下载模式生物选型指南>> 相关新闻 生物通微信公众号 生物通新浪微博 微信 新浪微博 我要投稿 搜索 国际 国内 人物 产业 热点 科普 热搜:慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染|聚乙二醇干扰素α-2b|HBsAg清除|淋巴细胞恢复|里程碑队列|功能治愈 热点排行 1人冠状动脉单细胞变异–增强子–基因图谱解析冠状动脉疾病非编码调控机制 2组织结构与细胞状态共进化驱动结直肠癌异质性及不良预后 3利用福克空间(Fock-space)共焦聚焦技术,通过500个光子实现量子增强的传感效果 4I-F3型CRISPR相关转座酶(CAST)RNA引导DNA整合的构象许可机制与TnsA计算设计激活 5华南中晚更新世丹尼索瓦亲和群体与未定古老型Homo谱系:广西穿山洞和龙穿洞牙齿的形态学与古蛋白组学证据 6内皮细胞对PIK3CAH1047R突变的上下文依赖性反应:分化状态决定血管病变易感性并揭示动脉内皮的内在抵抗 7耦合最小基耶夫链中的相干宇称振荡 今日动态 | 人才市场 | 新技术专栏 | 中国科学人 | 云展台 | BioHot | 云讲堂直播 | 会展中心 | 特价专栏 | 技术快讯 | 免费试用 版权所有 生物通 Copyright© eBiotrade.com, All Rights Reserved 联系信箱: 粤ICP备09063491号

supplementary_news.title: 中国生物制药:首个慢性乙型肝炎功能性治愈疗法贝普若韦生钠注射液在中国获批上市
supplementary_news.excerpt: 人民财讯11月27日电,中国生物制药在港交所公告,慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)同类首创功能性治愈疗法贝普若韦生钠注射液(商品名:贺舒可)已获得中国国家药监局批准上市,联合核苷(酸)类似物(NAs)用于慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染的功能性治愈,适用于已接受NAs治疗至少6个月、HBV DNA<90 IU/mL、乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg)≤3000 IU/mL、无肝硬化的慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染成人患者。
